definition_zh: 血统；世系；祖先的总称；家族出身；（生物）共同祖先关系
definition_en: the whole line of people from whom someone descends, the background this line gives them, or the shared origin of a group or species
core_image: 一条从先人延伸到自己脚下的血脉长线，重点在整条线，而不是线上某一个人
scene: 她做了基因检测，报告把她的血统追溯到东欧一座小村庄。She takes a DNA test, and the report traces her ancestry back to a small village in eastern Europe.
sceneCN: 这里 ancestry 是「作为整体的血统世系」（第 1 个义项：把许多代先人看作一条完整血脉）；句意：她做了基因检测，报告把她的血统世系追溯到东欧的一座小村庄。场景要点：检测报告、染色体图、迁徙路线、小村庄的地图标记、手指点着报告上的一条线。

pos.zh: 血统；世系；祖先的总称；出身

derivatives.zh: 在祖先方面；按祖先的方式

senses.title: The whole line of descent
senses.definition: the complete line of people from whom a person or group is descended, considered as one whole
senses.definitionCN: 某个人或群体所出自的、被当作一个整体的完整先人链条
senses.example: Her ancestry reaches back to fishing families on the northern coast.
senses.exampleCN: 她的血统可以追溯到北方海岸的渔民家庭。
senses.why: -ry makes a collective noun: it gathers many ancestors into one line, so ancestry names the whole rather than any single forebear.
senses.whyCN: -ry 构成集合名词：它把许多祖先聚成一条线，因此 ancestry 命名的是整体，而不是某一位先人。

senses.title: Family background as identity
senses.definition: a person's social, national, or ethnic background as defined by their forebears
senses.definitionCN: 由先人决定的个人社会、民族或族群背景
senses.example: The novelist wrote about her mixed ancestry with humor.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家用幽默的笔调写自己混合的血统背景。
senses.why: Once the line is a possession, it becomes part of identity; ancestry then answers 'where do you come from?' rather than 'who was your great-grandfather?'
senses.whyCN: 一旦这条线成为一种拥有物，它就变成身份的一部分；ancestry 于是回答“你从哪里来”，而不是“你的曾祖父是谁”。

senses.title: The traceable genealogical record
senses.definition: the chain of descent that can be followed through documents, names, and records
senses.definitionCN: 可以通过文件、姓名和记录逐环追查的血统链
senses.example: He spent ten years tracing his ancestry through parish registers.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了十年时间通过教区登记簿追溯自己的世系。
senses.why: A line can be followed link by link; when the links are documented, ancestry becomes the traceable genealogy itself.
senses.whyCN: 一条线可以一环一环地追下去；当这些环节有文献记录时，ancestry 就变成可追溯的谱系本身。

senses.title: Evolutionary common origin
senses.definition: the earlier population or species from which a present organism is descended
senses.definitionCN: 现存生物所由来的早期种群或物种
senses.example: The two bird species share a common ancestry in the southern continent.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种鸟在南半球大陆上拥有共同祖先。
senses.why: Biology borrows the family tree and replaces named relatives with populations; shared ancestry is the branching point where two lines separate.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了家族树，把有名字的亲属换成种群；共同血统就是两条谱系分开的那个分叉点。

senses.title: Inherited genetic material
senses.definition: the inherited genetic material of an individual or population
senses.definitionCN: 某个人或群体所继承的遗传物质
senses.example: The clinic uses ancestry to check for inherited risk variants.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所利用血统信息检查遗传性风险变异。
senses.why: In modern genetics the abstract line is measured as DNA; ancestry becomes the sum of inherited variants, a testable property rather than a family story.
senses.whyCN: 在现代遗传学里，抽象的血统线被测量为 DNA；ancestry 成为所继承变异的集合，是一种可检测的属性，而不是家族故事。

senses.title: Descent as a legal qualification
senses.definition: the fact of descent from a place or people, used to establish rights, citizenship, or status
senses.definitionCN: 从某地或某民族传下的事实，用来确立权利、公民身份或地位
senses.example: Citizenship was granted on the basis of ancestry rather than birthplace.
senses.exampleCN: 公民身份依据血统而非出生地授予。
senses.why: Law needs a rule that can be checked; descent from a national line becomes a formal qualification, so ancestry turns into evidence of belonging.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一条可核查的规则；从某国血统传下成为正式资格，ancestry 于是变成归属的证据。

senses.title: The source of a word, custom, or idea
senses.titleCN: 词语、习俗或观念的渊源
senses.definition: the origin or line of development of a word, custom, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 某个词语、习俗或观念的最初来源或发展线
senses.example: The ancestry of the proverb can be traced through three languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这句谚语的渊源可以穿过三种语言追溯出来。
senses.why: Anything that develops can be given a line of predecessors; ancestry then means 'the chain of earlier sources' rather than biological descent.
senses.whyCN: 任何会发展的事物都可以被安排一条前身线；ancestry 于是表示“更早来源的链条”，而不是生物血统。

senses.title: The pedigree of domesticated stock
senses.definition: the line of forebears of a domesticated animal or plant, especially as recorded by breeders
senses.definitionCN: 家养动物或植物的先代链条，尤指育种者记录下来的谱系
senses.example: The breeder keeps careful records of the herd's ancestry.
senses.exampleCN: 育种者仔细记录牛群的谱系。
senses.why: Selective breeding treats animals like families; the pedigree is literally an ancestry record, so the word applies to stock as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 选育把动物当作家族来对待；血统记录字面上就是 ancestry record，因此这个词也适用于家畜，而不只适用于人。

senses.title: The ancestors taken together
senses.definition: the ancestors of a person taken together, especially when they are addressed as a body in ceremony or literature
senses.definitionCN: 把某人的祖先们聚在一起看待，尤指在仪式或文学中被作为一个整体称呼时
senses.example: The ceremony calls on the ancestry to witness the marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式召唤祖先们来见证这场婚礼。
senses.why: The collective noun can be personified: the line stands in for the dead as a group, so ancestry is occasionally used where ancestor(s) would be concrete.
senses.whyCN: 这个集合名词可以被拟人化：整条线代表死者群体，因此 ancestry 偶尔会出现在本可以用具体 ancestor(s) 的地方。

intro.en: Ancestry is the collective and abstract noun beside ancestor, not a variant spelling of it. Old French ancesserie, built on ancestre with the suffix -erie, names the whole line or stock; English -ry keeps that collective force, and the spelling was later reshaped under the influence of ancestor. The base goes back to Latin antecessor 'fore-goer' (ante 'before' + cedere 'to go'). Ancient is a look-alike from ante + -anus, not from antiquus; descendant is from scandere 'to climb', not from cedere.
intro.cn: ancestry 是 ancestor 旁边的集合/抽象名词，不是它的拼写变体。古法语 ancesserie 在 ancestre 上加 -erie，指整条世系或整个血统；英语 -ry 保留这种集合义，后来拼写又受 ancestor 影响而调整。基础词可追溯到拉丁语 antecessor“先行者”（ante“前”+ cedere“走”）。ancient 是来自 ante + -anus 的形近词，并非来自 antiquus；descendant 来自 scandere“爬”，并非来自 cedere。

items.en: First recorded in English as auncestrie, 'series or line of ancestors, descent from ancestors'. The word names the line, not one person in it.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为 auncestrie，意为“祖先的序列或世系、从祖先传下”。这个词命名的是整条线，而不是线中的某个人。

items.en: From Old French ancesserie 'ancestry, ancestors, forefathers', formed on ancestre 'ancestor'. The French noun already had a collective sense.
items.cn: 来自古法语 ancesserie“血统、祖先、父辈”，由 ancestre“祖先”构成。这个法语名词本身已带集合义。

items.en: The French suffix -erie (English -ry) forms nouns of state, collection, or place. Added to ancestre it does not name one forebear but the whole stock or line; English later respelled the word under the influence of ancestor.
items.cn: 法语后缀 -erie（英语 -ry）构成状态、集合或地点名词。加在 ancestre 上，它不指某一位先人，而指整个血统或世系；英语后来受 ancestor 影响改写了拼写。

items.en: ancestre goes back to Late Latin antecessor 'predecessor', literally 'fore-goer', from antecedere 'to precede' = ante 'before' + cedere 'to go'.
items.cn: ancestre 可追溯到晚期拉丁语 antecessor“前任”，字面义“先行者”，来自 antecedere“走在前面”= ante“前”+ cedere“走”。

items.en: ante is traced to PIE *ant- 'front, forehead' and cedere to *ked- 'to go, yield'. The reconstructions are standard, but the exact route through Late Latin is not fully certain.
items.cn: ante 被追溯到原始印欧语 *ant-“前面、额头”，cedere 追溯到 *ked-“走、让步”。这些重构是通行的，但经过晚期拉丁语的具体路径并非完全确定。

items.en: Ancestry keeps the abstract or collective meaning, while ancestor is the countable person. It is not related to ancient as a derivative: ancient comes from ante + -anus, and antique is the word from antiquus. The opposite-direction cedere relative is successor, not descendant.
items.cn: ancestry 保留抽象或集合义，而 ancestor 是可数的人。它不是 ancient 的派生词：ancient 来自 ante + -anus，来自 antiquus 的是 antique。反向的 cedere 同根词是 successor，不是 descendant。

note.en: The first group separates the person noun, the adjective, and the look-alike from ancestry; the second compares words about lines, origins, and inheritance.
note.cn: 第一组把人物名词、形容词和形近词同 ancestry 分开；第二组比较关于世系、来源与继承的词。

entries.definition: one forebear. Ancestry is the whole line; ancestor is one countable link in it.
entries.definitionCN: 一位先人。ancestry 是整条线；ancestor 是线中一个可数的环节。

entries.definition: relating to ancestors. It describes a thing or place; ancestry is the noun for the line itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与祖先有关的。它描述某物或某地；ancestry 是表示这条线本身的名词。

entries.definition: belonging to the distant past. It shares the *ant- 'before' root but is not a form of ancestry, and it does not come from antiquus.
entries.definitionCN: 属于遥远过去的。它共享 *ant-“前”词根，但不是 ancestry 的形式，也不来自 antiquus。

entries.definition: a female ancestor. It is a derived person noun, not the collective line.
entries.definitionCN: 女祖先。它是派生的人物名词，不是集合性的世系。

entries.definition: a direct line of descent from an ancestor, especially a documented or formal one. It often stresses noble or official descent, while ancestry is broader and more personal.
entries.definitionCN: 从某位祖先传下的直系血统，尤指有记录或正式的血统。它常强调贵族或官方世系，而 ancestry 更宽泛、更个人化。

entries.definition: the fact of coming from a particular ancestor or group. It is the relation viewed from the descendant's side; ancestry is the total stock behind that relation.
entries.definitionCN: 出自某位祖先或某个群体的事实。它是从后代一方看的关系；ancestry 则是这一关系背后的全部血统储备。

entries.definition: the study or record of family lines. It is the research or chart, while ancestry is the biological or social fact being researched.
entries.definitionCN: 对家族世系的研究或记录。它指研究或谱表，而 ancestry 是被研究的生物或社会事实。

entries.definition: the traditions, language, and property inherited from a group. It includes culture and things, while ancestry is specifically the line of people.
entries.definitionCN: 从某个群体继承的传统、语言和财产。它包含文化与实物，而 ancestry 特指人的血统线。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ancestor plus the French collective suffix -erie/-ry, the contrast with the countable ancestor, and the near words lineage, descent and genealogy.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：ancestor 加法语集合后缀 -erie/-ry，与可数 ancestor 的对比，以及 lineage、descent、genealogy 这组近义词。

normal.en: ancestry is ancestor + the French collective suffix -erie/-ry; the suffix gathers many ancestors into one line.
normal.cn: ancestry 是 ancestor 加法语集合后缀 -erie/-ry；这个后缀把许多祖先聚成一条线。

normal.en: Ancestor names one person; ancestry names the whole stock or line, so the two are not interchangeable.
normal.cn: ancestor 指一个人；ancestry 指整个血统或世系，两者不能互换。

normal.en: The spelling was reshaped by ancestor, which is why ancestry looks as if it contains the whole noun ancestor.
normal.cn: 拼写受 ancestor 影响而调整，所以 ancestry 看起来像把整个 ancestor 包了进去。

normal.en: Ancient is not the adjective of ancestry; the adjective is ancestral. Ancient comes from ante + -anus, while antique comes from antiquus.
normal.cn: ancient 不是 ancestry 的形容词；形容词是 ancestral。ancient 来自 ante + -anus，而 antique 来自 antiquus。

normal.en: Lineage stresses a documented line, descent the relation from the descendant's side, and genealogy the study or chart; ancestry is the broad fact behind all three.
normal.cn: lineage 强调有记录的世系，descent 强调从后代一方看的关系，genealogy 指研究或谱表；ancestry 是三者背后的宽泛事实。

abstract.en: Imagine a rope braided from many strands: each strand is an ancestor, the braided rope is ancestry.
abstract.cn: 想象一根由许多股编成的绳：每一股是一个 ancestor，编成的整根绳就是 ancestry。

abstract.en: A river delta: many upstream streams feed one channel; the streams are ancestors and their combined watershed is ancestry.
abstract.cn: 一片河口三角洲：上游许多溪流汇入一条水道；溪流是 ancestors，它们合起来的分水岭就是 ancestry。

abstract.en: A pedigree chart: one box is a person, but the connected chain of boxes is the ancestry.
abstract.cn: 一张谱系图：一个方框是一个人，而连起来的整串方框才是 ancestry。

examples.en: She discovered that her ancestry includes both farmers and sailors.
examples.cn: 她发现自己的血统里既有农民也有水手。

examples.en: Researchers use DNA to estimate shared ancestry among populations.
examples.cn: 研究人员用 DNA 估计群体间的共同血统。

examples.en: The law grants citizenship on the basis of ancestry.
examples.cn: 这项法律依据血统授予公民身份。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺家谱」——‘俺’家的谱系一代代传下来 → ancestry 血统、世系（只借音，不表词源）

root: 古法语 ancesserie < ancestre < 拉丁语 antecessor“先行者”（ante 前 + cedere 走）；-ry/-erie 使具体先人变成“血统总体、世系”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of ancestry all treat descent as a whole: the line itself, the identity it gives, its traceable record, a species' branching point, its DNA, a legal qualification, a cultural source, a pedigree, and the ancestors personified.
sensesIntro.cn: ancestry 的九个义项都把血统当作整体来处理：这条线本身、它带来的身份、可追溯的记录、物种的分叉点、它的 DNA、法律资格、文化渊源、谱系记录，以及被拟人化的祖先群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the whole braided line of descent, seen as one thing rather than as separate people.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整条编合起来的血统线，被当作一个整体，而不是分开的许多人。

branches.en: THE LINE AS A WHOLE: the abstract descent, and the same ancestors personified as a body.
branches.cn: 作为整体的线：抽象的血统世系，以及被拟人化为群体的同一批祖先。

branches.en: IDENTITY AND STATUS: background becomes personal identity, and descent becomes a legal qualification.
branches.cn: 身份与地位：背景成为个人身份，血统成为法律资格。

branches.en: RECORDED LINES: parish registers trace a family, and breeders' records trace a pedigree.
branches.cn: 被记录的线：教区登记簿追溯家族，育种记录追溯谱系。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: populations share a branching origin, and modern genetics measures that origin as DNA.
branches.cn: 生物学：种群共享一个分叉来源，现代遗传学把这一来源测量为 DNA。

branches.en: CULTURAL SOURCE: words, customs and ideas can have a chain of earlier sources too.
branches.cn: 文化渊源：词语、习俗和观念也可以有一条更早来源的链条。

intro.en: Ancestry is ancestre + the French suffix -erie, continued in English as -ry. The suffix is the key: it changes a countable person noun into a collective or state noun. The base ancestre is the same word that gives ancestor, and it goes back to Latin antecessor.
intro.cn: ancestry 是 ancestre 加法语后缀 -erie，在英语中延续为 -ry。关键就在这个后缀：它把可数的人物名词变成集合或状态名词。基础词 ancestre 与 ancestor 同源，可追溯到拉丁语 antecessor。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is antecessor 'fore-goer' from antecedere (ante 'before' + cedere 'to go'). Cedere also gives predecessor and successor, but not descendant, which belongs to scandere 'to climb'. The deepest *ant- and *ked- roots are reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 antecessor“先行者”，来自 antecedere（ante“前”+ cedere“走”）。cedere 也构成 predecessor 和 successor，但不构成 descendant，后者属于 scandere“爬”。最深层的 *ant- 与 *ked- 词根是重构形式。

items.meaningCN: 血统；世系（-ry 构成集合或状态名词）
items.example: The census records are useful for studying ancestry.
items.exampleCN: 人口普查记录对研究血统很有用。

items.structure: ante- (before) + cedere (go), through Late Latin antecessor
items.meaning: one who goes before; a forebear
items.meaningCN: 先行者；祖先（ante- 前 + cedere 走）
items.example: Every ancestor in the chart has a birth record.
items.exampleCN: 谱系图中的每一位祖先都有出生记录。

items.meaningCN: 祖先的；与先人有关的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The ancestral house is now a small museum.
items.exampleCN: 那座祖宅现在是一座小博物馆。

items.example: The ancestress left a diary that covers forty years.
items.exampleCN: 这位女祖先留下了一本跨越四十年的日记。

items.meaning: in a way that relates to ancestors
items.meaningCN: 在祖先方面；按祖先的方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The family was ancestrally tied to the same valley.
items.exampleCN: 这个家族在血统上与同一座山谷相连。

items.meaningCN: 前事；先行者（ante- 前 + cedere 走 + -ent）
items.example: The custom has an antecedent in an older harvest rite.
items.exampleCN: 这一习俗的前身是一种更古老的丰收仪式。

items.meaning: someone or something that came before
items.meaningCN: 前任；前身（prae- 前 + de- 离 + cedere 走）
items.example: The predecessor of the archive was a private collection.
items.exampleCN: 这个档案馆的前身是一批私人收藏。

items.meaningCN: 继任者；后继者（sub- 后 + cedere 走）
items.example: The successor inherited the same record-keeping duty.
items.exampleCN: 继任者继承了他们同样的记录职责。

items.structure: de- (down) + scandere (climb); not a cedere word
items.meaning: a person or thing that comes from an earlier one
items.meaningCN: 后代；衍生物（de- 下 + scandere 爬；不是 cedere 同根词）
items.example: The descendants of the first settlers still live nearby.
items.exampleCN: 最早定居者的后代仍住在附近。

items.structure: Latin ante (before) + -anus, through Vulgar Latin *anteanus; not from antiquus
items.meaningCN: 古老的；古代的（ante 前 + -anus；并非来自 antiquus）
items.example: The ancient records were copied onto new paper.
items.exampleCN: 那些古老的记录被抄到了新纸上。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb; source of descend and descendant, not of ancestry
latinEntries.meaningCN: 爬；攀登（descend/descendant 的来源，不是 ancestry 的来源）

definition_zh: 辅助的；附属的；补充的；（名词）助手；辅助人员
definition_en: providing necessary support to the primary activities of an organization or process; subordinate or auxiliary
core_image: 主菜旁的小配菜：本身不是主角，缺了它整顿饭就不完整
scene: 手术室外，护士正准备器械。The hospital hired ancillary staff to support the surgeons during long operations.
sceneCN: 这里 ancillary 是「辅助的、从属的」（第 1 个义项：为主要活动提供支持）；句意为：医院聘请辅助人员在外科医生进行长时间手术时提供支持。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语借词，义为「女仆；帮手」，是 ancillary 的直接词源
罕见派生，义为「辅助性；从属性」

senses.title: Providing support to the main activity
senses.definition: giving help or support to the primary work of a person, organization, or system
senses.definitionCN: 为个人、组织或系统的主要工作提供帮助或支持
senses.example: Ancillary departments keep the main office running smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 辅助部门使主办公室顺利运转。
senses.why: A servant exists to serve the master's work, so the meaning grew from serving to supporting.
senses.whyCN: ancilla 本义是婢女，婢女的存在是为主人的工作服务，词义由此从「服侍」引申为「辅助」。

senses.title: Subordinate in importance or rank
senses.definition: less important than something else and dependent on it
senses.definitionCN: 比另一事物重要性低，且依附于它
senses.example: The paperwork is ancillary to the actual teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 文书工作从属于真正的教学。
senses.why: A servant holds a lower position, so the word extended to anything of secondary standing.
senses.whyCN: 婢女地位低于主人，因此词义延伸到一切处于次要地位的事物。

senses.title: Additional but necessary
senses.definition: added to something else to complete or extend it
senses.definitionCN: 添加在另一事物之上，使之完整或扩展
senses.example: The airline profits from ancillary fees like baggage charges.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司从行李费等附加费用中获利。
senses.why: Support services attach themselves alongside the core, just as extras attach to a main purchase.
senses.whyCN: 辅助服务附着于核心业务之旁，正如附加项目附着于主消费之上。

senses.title: A person who provides support
senses.definition: a worker whose job is to assist the main professional staff
senses.definitionCN: 职责是协助主要专业人员的工作人员
senses.example: The lab hired two ancillaries to prepare samples.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室雇了两名辅助人员来准备样本。
senses.why: The noun keeps the original Latin sense of a serving person, applied to modern workplaces.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了拉丁语「服侍者」的本义，被应用到现代职场语境。

senses.title: Something accessory to a main thing
senses.definition: a thing that is subordinate or accessory to something else
senses.definitionCN: 从属于另一事物或作为其配件的事物
senses.example: Legal work is often an ancillary of the merger process.
senses.exampleCN: 法律事务常常是并购流程的附属环节。
senses.why: What serves the master can be a person or a task, so the noun widened to things.
senses.whyCN: 为主人服务者可以是人也可以是事务，名词词义因此扩展到事物。

senses.title: Relating to subordination in law or contracts
senses.definition: in law, secondary to and dependent on a principal agreement or document
senses.definitionCN: 法律语境中，从属于并依附于主协议或主文件
senses.example: The guarantee clause is ancillary to the main contract.
senses.exampleCN: 担保条款从属于主合同。
senses.why: Law borrows the master–servant hierarchy to rank documents by importance.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用「主人—仆人」的等级关系给文件按重要性排序，附属性由此而来。

senses.title: Ancillary to something: functioning in service of it
senses.definition: existing or functioning in order to serve a larger purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为服务于更大的目的而存在或运作
senses.example: Every ancillary to the festival, from parking to security, was planned early.
senses.exampleCN: 为音乐节服务的各项配套，从停车到安保，都早早做了规划。
senses.why: The image of the servant standing by for orders becomes purpose-built support systems.
senses.whyCN: 婢女在旁待命的画面，转化为围绕目标建立的配套支持体系。

senses.title: Supporting scientific or technical work
senses.definition: used to describe equipment or industries that support a main technical process
senses.definitionCN: 形容支持主要技术流程的设备或行业
senses.example: Ancillary industries supply parts to the car plant.
senses.exampleCN: 配套产业为汽车厂供应零部件。
senses.why: Machines also have servants; the supporting equipment image comes from the serving relation.
senses.whyCN: 机器也有自己的「仆人」，配套设备的意象同样源于「服侍」关系。

intro.en: Ancillary descends from a humble Latin household word for a maidservant, rising through the idea of service to mean whatever supports the main work.
intro.cn: ancillary 源自拉丁语一个指「婢女」的家常用词，经由「服侍」之意上升为「辅助主要工作之物」。

items.en: The noun ancilla meant a maidservant, a female household servant; its origin before Latin is uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 ancilla 意为「婢女、家内女仆」；其更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The adjective ancillaris was formed with the suffix -aris, meaning relating to a servant or serving.
items.cn: 后拉丁时期用后缀 -aris 构成形容词 ancillaris，义为「仆人的；服侍性的」。

items.en: English adopted the adjective as ancillary around the 1620s, first in the literal sense of serving like a handmaid.
items.cn: 英语约在 17 世纪 20 年代借入 ancillary，最初用于「如婢女般服侍」的本义。

items.en: The sense widened from personal service to any subordinate or supporting function.
items.cn: 词义从「人身服侍」扩展到「任何从属或辅助性职能」。

items.en: Today ancillary chiefly describes support roles, services, and industries, and can also name the supporting people or things themselves.
items.cn: 如今 ancillary 主要形容辅助角色、服务与产业，也可名词化指辅助人员或配套事物。

note.en: The words below are grouped by spelling kinship and by closeness of meaning to ancillary.
note.cn: 下面按拼写亲缘与语义接近两组列出与 ancillary 相关的词。

entries.definition: the Latin source word, meaning a maidservant
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语源头词，义为「婢女」，与 ancillary 同根

entries.definition: situated in the armpit; relating to an axil in botany
entries.definitionCN: 腋下的；（植物学）腋生的，与 ancillary 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: providing supplementary help, especially extra troops or verbs
entries.definitionCN: 辅助的；补充的（如辅助部队、助动词），与 ancillary 同源近义但侧重增援

entries.definition: lower in rank or importance
entries.definitionCN: 级别或重要性较低的，从属的

entries.definition: added to complete or extend a thing
entries.definitionCN: 补充性的，用来补足或扩展主体

entries.definition: a thing that adds to or completes something else
entries.definitionCN: 附件；配件，强调附加而非从属

normalIntro.en: These memory hooks are built on the real Latin root ancilla and real word family.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆锚点基于真实的拉丁词根 ancilla 与真实词族。

normal.en: ancilla = Latin maidservant; an ancillary worker is like a helper beside the master.
normal.cn: ancilla 是拉丁语「婢女」；ancillary 人员就像主人身旁的帮手。

normal.en: Same root family: ancilla → ancillaris → ancillary, a straight line from servant to support.
normal.cn: 同根词链：ancilla → ancillaris → ancillary，从「仆人」一路到「辅助」。

normal.en: Auxiliary troops and ancillary staff both come from servant-related roots.
normal.cn: auxiliary（辅助部队）与 ancillary（辅助人员）的词源都与「仆役」相关。

normal.en: The phrase ancillary to marks what serves what, like ancillary to the main task.
normal.cn: 搭配 ancillary to 标明谁服务于谁，如「从属于主要任务」。

normal.en: In hospitals, ancillary services mean the departments behind the doctors.
normal.cn: 在医院里，ancillary services 指医生身后的各个支持科室。

abstract.en: Picture a maid quietly arranging the room while the master works: she is ancillary.
abstract.cn: 想象主人工作时女仆在一旁悄悄整理房间：她就是 ancillary（辅助者）。

abstract.en: See the main dish at the center of a table with small side dishes orbiting it, each one ancillary.
abstract.cn: 想象主菜在餐桌中央，小配菜围绕四周，每一样都是 ancillary（配套）。

abstract.en: Feel the word tilting sideways: the main beam stands upright, ancillary beams lean in to hold it.
abstract.cn: 感受这个词的「斜倚感」：主梁直立，辅助的梁斜撑在旁，即为 ancillary。

examples.en: The university cut ancillary services to save money.
examples.cn: 大学削减了辅助服务以节省开支。

examples.en: Transport is ancillary to the main business of publishing.
examples.cn: 运输从属于出版这一主营业务。

examples.en: Ancillary staff keep the hospital clean and running.
examples.cn: 辅助人员保持医院的清洁与运转。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺尽力辅助」——俺虽是配角，但尽力辅助主角，正是 ancillary（辅助的）的画面。

root: 拉丁语 ancilla（婢女，来源不确定）+ 后缀 -aris（属于……的）→ 拉丁语 ancillaris「仆人的」→ 英语 ancillary。词义核心是「服侍 → 辅助」。

sensesIntro.en: From the Latin image of a maidservant, the word fans out into adjectival senses of support, subordination, and supplementation, plus noun uses for the people and things that serve.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拉丁语「婢女」的画面出发，词义铺展为「支持、从属、补充」等形容词义项，以及指代辅助者与配套事物的名词义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the servant standing beside the master's work
core.cn: 核心意象：站在主人工作之旁的仆役

intro.cn: ancillary 的词族不大但脉络清晰：一个拉丁名词加形容词、名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin built the family on ancilla with the adjective suffix -aris.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语以 ancilla 为基础，用形容词后缀 -aris 构建了这个词族。

items.example: The ancilla kept the Roman household in order.
items.exampleCN: 婢女维持罗马家庭的秩序。

items.meaning: of or belonging to a servant
items.example: Munera ancillaria were the servant's daily tasks.
items.exampleCN: ancillaria 指仆人的日常职责。

items.meaning: relating to; a place or collection
items.meaningCN: 与……有关的；（名词）场所或集合
items.example: Honorary and salary share this productive suffix.
items.exampleCN: honorary 与 salary 都用了这一能产后缀。

items.example: The opening an- of ancilla is generally treated as part of the whole root.
items.exampleCN: ancilla 开头的 an- 一般视为整个词根的一部分。

items.meaning: the serving element of the word
items.meaningCN: 词中承载「服侍」义的词干
items.example: Ancillary and ancilla share the stem -cill-.
items.exampleCN: ancillary 与 ancilla 共享词干 -cill-。

items.example: Auxiliary verbs help the main verb.
Servile duties once meant household service.
items.exampleCN: servile duties 曾指家内仆役工作。

items.example: A subsidiary company supports the parent firm.
Car accessories are ancillary products in a loose sense.
items.exampleCN: 汽车配件宽泛地说是附加产品。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语原词借入英语，义为「婢女；女仆」

definition_zh: 麻醉剂；麻醉药；（形容词）麻醉的；使失去感觉的
definition_en: a substance that causes loss of sensation; relating to or causing anesthesia
core_image: 一支针管让疼痛沉睡：身体还在，感觉先离场
scene: 牙医举起注射器，病人闭上眼睛。The dentist gave her an anesthetic before pulling the wisdom tooth.
sceneCN: 这里 anesthetic 是「麻醉剂」（第 1 个义项：使失去感觉的物质）；句意为：牙医在拔智齿前给她注射了麻醉剂。

derivatives.zh: anesthetic 的状态名词，义为「麻醉；麻木」

senses.title: A drug causing loss of sensation
senses.definition: a substance given to a patient to prevent pain during medical procedures
senses.definitionCN: 给病人使用以在医疗过程中防止疼痛的物质
senses.example: The surgeon chose a general anesthetic for the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生为这次手术选择了全身麻醉剂。
senses.why: The Greek root means without sensation, so the noun names the thing that removes feeling.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根义为「没有感觉」，名词即指去除感觉之物。

senses.title: Loss of feeling produced by a drug
senses.definition: the state of temporary lost sensation produced by such a substance
senses.definitionCN: 此类物质造成的暂时性感觉丧失状态
senses.example: She was under anesthetic for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她在麻醉状态下度过了三小时。
senses.why: The drug and the state it produces share one word, as cause and effect merge.
senses.whyCN: 药物与其产生的状态共用一词，因果合于一体。

senses.title: Relating to anesthesia
senses.definition: connected with or used in anesthesia
senses.definitionCN: 与麻醉相关或用于麻醉的
senses.example: Anesthetic drugs require careful dosing.
senses.exampleCN: 麻醉药物需要精确控制剂量。
senses.why: Once the noun existed, the adjective naturally described everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 名词确立后，形容词自然用于描述与之相关的一切。

senses.title: Numbed or dulled in feeling
senses.definition: unable to feel physical sensation in part or all of the body
senses.definitionCN: 身体局部或全部无法感受物理刺激
senses.example: His fingers stayed anesthetic after the cold night.
senses.exampleCN: 寒冷一夜之后，他的手指依然麻木。
senses.why: Sensation removed by cold feels like sensation removed by a drug, so the adjective spread.
senses.whyCN: 寒冷夺走感觉如同药物夺走感觉，形容词因此扩散使用。

senses.title: Emotionally deadening
senses.titleCN: （比喻）令人麻木的；麻痹情感的
senses.definition: dulling emotional response or awareness
senses.definitionCN: 使情感反应或意识变得迟钝
senses.example: The constant bad news had an anesthetic effect on the public.
senses.exampleCN: 接连的坏消息对公众产生了麻醉般的效果。
senses.why: Loss of feeling extends from the skin to the heart, from body to mind.
senses.whyCN: 「失去感觉」从皮肤延伸到内心，从身体扩展到心灵。

senses.title: A local numbing agent
senses.definition: an anesthetic applied to one small area rather than the whole body
senses.definitionCN: 只作用于身体局部而非全身的麻醉剂
senses.example: The cut was stitched with a local anesthetic only.
senses.exampleCN: 缝 合伤口时只用了局部麻醉剂。
senses.why: Sensation can be switched off in one room of the body while the rest stays awake.
senses.whyCN: 感觉可以在身体的「一个房间」被关闭，而其余部分保持清醒。

senses.title: A general anesthetic: full unconsciousness
senses.definition: an anesthetic that puts the whole body and mind to sleep for surgery
senses.definitionCN: 使全身与意识进入睡眠以施行手术的麻醉剂
senses.example: General anesthetics carry higher risks than local ones.
senses.exampleCN: 全身麻醉剂比局部麻醉风险更高。
senses.why: When the whole house sleeps, the anesthesia is general rather than local.
senses.whyCN: 当整座「房子」都睡着，麻醉便是全身性而非局部性。

senses.title: An anesthetic to something: a soothing distraction
senses.definition: something that numbs worry or pain without solving it
senses.definitionCN: 麻痹忧虑或痛苦而不解决问题的事物
senses.example: Entertainment became an anesthetic to his anxiety.
senses.exampleCN: 娱乐成了麻痹他焦虑的麻醉剂。
senses.why: What quiets pain temporarily becomes, in metaphor, any numbing comfort.
senses.whyCN: 能暂时止痛之物，在比喻中泛化为一切麻木性的慰藉。

intro.en: Anesthetic is a modern scientific coinage built from Greek parts that say exactly what it does: no sensation.
intro.cn: anesthetic 是用希腊语部件拼装的现代科学造词，字面即「没有感觉」。

items.en: The root *dhē- meant to set or place, giving Greek aisthēsis, sensation, through a sense of perceiving what is presented.
items.cn: 原始印欧词根 *dhē- 义为「放置」，经由「感知所呈现之物」一义发展出希腊语 aisthēsis（感觉）。一般认为此联系成立。

items.en: Anaisthēsia meant insensibility, from ana- (without) plus aisthēsis (sensation).
items.cn: 希腊语 anaisthēsia 意为「无感觉」，由 ana-（无）加 aisthēsis（感觉）构成。

items.en: Oliver Wendell Holmes coined anesthesia in 1846, the year ether anesthesia was first publicly demonstrated.
items.cn: 1846 年乙醚麻醉首次公开展示，同年奥利弗·温德尔·霍姆斯创造了 anesthesia 一词。

items.en: The agent noun anesthetic quickly followed, and British spelling kept the extra a as anaesthetic.
items.cn: 表 agent 的 anesthetic 随之出现；英式拼写保留多余的 a，作 anaesthetic。

items.en: Today anesthetic names the drugs, the state, and, as an adjective, everything numbing.
items.cn: 如今 anesthetic 既指麻醉药物与状态，作形容词也指一切令人麻木之物。

note.en: Grouped by shared Greek roots and by nearby meanings of numbing and sensation.
note.cn: 按共享的希腊词根与「麻痹、感觉」的近义关系分组。

entries.definition: the state of lost sensation; the source noun of anesthetic
entries.definitionCN: 感觉丧失状态，anesthetic 的源名词，同根

entries.definition: relating to beauty or artistic taste
entries.definitionCN: 审美的；美学的，与 anesthetic 只是部分拼写相近，词根同出 aisthēsis 但词义不同

entries.definition: experiencing one sense through another, as hearing colors
entries.definitionCN: 联觉的（如听见颜色），共享 aisthēsis 词根

entries.definition: a drug that relieves pain without full loss of sensation
entries.definitionCN: 止痛药，止痛但不完全消除感觉

entries.definition: a drug that calms rather than numbs
entries.definitionCN: 镇静剂，作用是安抚而非消除感觉

entries.definition: causing loss of physical or emotional feeling
entries.definitionCN: 使麻木的，日常用语的近义表达

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek roots ana- and aisthēsis.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的希腊词根 ana- 与 aisthēsis。

normal.en: ana- = without; aisthēsis = sensation; so anesthetic is literally without-sensation.
normal.cn: ana- 表「无」，aisthēsis 表「感觉」，anesthetic 字面即「无感觉」。

normal.en: Same root: esthetic deals with what the senses perceive, anesthetic removes perception.
normal.cn: 同根词：esthetic 处理感官所感知之物，anesthetic 则移除感知。

normal.en: Synesthesia joins senses, anesthesia cuts them off.
normal.cn: synesthesia（联觉）让感官相连，anesthesia 则切断感官。

normal.en: British spelling anaesthetic keeps two a's, like anaemia keeps its second a.
normal.cn: 英式拼写 anaesthetic 有两个 a，与 anaemia 的双 a 一致。

normal.en: The family grows: anesthetic → anesthetize → anesthetist.
normal.cn: 词族可延伸：anesthetic → anesthetize（使麻醉）→ anesthetist（麻醉师）。

abstract.en: Picture feeling draining out of your arm like water from a leaking tube.
abstract.cn: 想象感觉像水从漏管中一样从手臂里流走。

abstract.en: See a dimmer switch turning sensation down to zero before an operation.
abstract.cn: 想象手术前有一个调光开关把「感觉」一路调到零。

abstract.en: Feel cotton wrapping your mind: soft, distant, unable to register pain.
abstract.cn: 感受棉花裹住头脑：柔软、遥远、无法感知疼痛。

examples.en: The operation was performed under a general anesthetic.
examples.cn: 手术在全身麻醉下进行。

examples.en: Apply the anesthetic cream before the injection.
examples.cn: 注射前先涂麻醉药膏。

examples.en: The news had an anesthetic effect on the exhausted city.
examples.cn: 消息对精疲力竭的城市产生了麻木般的效果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺没感觉」——打了麻醉针，俺没感觉了，正好对应 anesthetic 的字面义「无感觉」。

items.example: Anatomy originally meant cutting up.
Aesthetics is the philosophy of perception and beauty.

items.exampleCN: synesthesia 将两种感觉合并为一种体验。

senses.title: Resembling an angel in beauty or purity
senses.definition: having the beauty or purity associated with angels

senses.exampleCN: 她有一张画家们都喜爱的天使般的面孔。
senses.why: The angel is the picture of perfect purity, so faces and smiles that look heavenly take its name.
senses.whyCN: 天使是纯洁的完美图景，故圣洁美好的面容与微笑借其得名。

senses.title: Kind and good-natured
senses.definition: showing great kindness or goodness of character
senses.definitionCN: 表现出极大的善良或品行上的美好
senses.example: He was angelic to strangers, always ready to help.
senses.exampleCN: 他对陌生人极为友善，总是乐于相助。
senses.why: Angels are messengers of goodwill, so gentle people are said to share their nature.
senses.whyCN: 天使是善意的信使，因此温柔的人被说成具有天使般的本性。

senses.title: Relating to actual angels
senses.definition: belonging to or connected with angels as spiritual beings
senses.definitionCN: 属于天使或与作为灵性存在的天使相关
senses.example: Medieval art devoted whole pages to angelic hierarchies.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪艺术用整页篇幅描绘天使的等级体系。
senses.why: Before metaphor, the adjective simply pointed at angels themselves.
senses.whyCN: 在比喻用法之前，这个形容词本就直指天使本身。

senses.title: Heavenly in sound
senses.definition: used of voices or music that sound pure and heavenly
senses.definitionCN: 形容声音或音乐纯净如天籁
senses.example: An angelic choir filled the cathedral with song.
senses.exampleCN: 天使般的合唱让大教堂充满歌声。
senses.why: Heaven is imagined as perfect music, so the purest voices borrow its sound.
senses.whyCN: 天堂被想象为完美的音乐，因此最纯净的嗓音借用其声。

senses.title: Sweetly innocent, sometimes deceptively so
senses.titleCN: 天真无邪的（有时貌似如此）
senses.definition: looking innocent or sweet, sometimes while hiding the opposite
senses.definitionCN: 看似天真甜美，有时却藏有反的一面
senses.example: With angelic innocence he asked who had broken the vase.
senses.exampleCN: 他一脸天真无邪地问是谁打碎了花瓶。
senses.why: The halo image can be worn like a mask, so the word gains an ironic edge.
senses.whyCN: 光环可以被当作面具佩戴，这个词因此带上反讽色彩。

senses.title: Extraordinarily patient
senses.definition: showing almost superhuman patience
senses.definitionCN: 表现出近乎超人的耐心
senses.example: She showed angelic patience with the noisy children.
senses.exampleCN: 她对吵闹的孩子表现出天使般的耐心。
senses.why: Angels never lose their temper, so limitless patience is called theirs.
senses.whyCN: 天使从不发怒，所以无限的耐心被称为天使的耐心。

senses.title: Devotional or spiritual in tone
senses.definition: carrying a spiritual or sacred atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 带有灵性或神圣的氛围
senses.example: The composer wrote an angelic motet for the feast.
senses.exampleCN: 作曲家为节庆谱写了一首圣洁的经文歌。
senses.why: Anything touching the heavenly realm takes on the adjective of its messengers.
senses.whyCN: 一切触及天国领域之物都带上其信使的形容词。

senses.title: Angelically good behavior in children
senses.definition: used of children who behave perfectly well
senses.definitionCN: 形容表现得无可挑剔的孩童
senses.example: The twins were angelic all through the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 双胞胎在整个仪式上都很乖巧。
senses.why: The contrast between angelic looks and childish mischief makes the word a favorite, and slightly wry, praise.
senses.whyCN: 天使外貌与孩童顽皮的反差使这个词成为略带调侃的赞美。

intro.en: Angelic travels from a Greek word for messenger through Latin and French to become English's adjective for the heaven-sent.
intro.cn: angelic 从一个希腊语「信使」词出发，经拉丁语与法语，成为英语中形容天国使者的形容词。

items.en: The root *her- meant to move or fit together, generally reconstructed as the source of Greek angelos.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧词根 *her-（移动、配合）是希腊语 angelos 的来源，属重构形式。

items.en: Angelos meant messenger; in the Greek Bible it named divine messengers from God.
items.cn: 希腊语 angelos 意为「信使」；在希腊文圣经中特指上帝派来的使者。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as angelus, keeping both the plain and the religious senses.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 angelus，同时保留了普通义与宗教义。

items.en: Old French received angele, later ange, and built angelique from the Latin form.
items.cn: 古法语承接为 angele（后作 ange），并从拉丁词形派生出 angelique。

items.en: English took angel from French and formed angelic from the Latin adjective in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语从法语借得 angel，十六世纪又依拉丁形容词形造出 angelic。

note.en: Grouped by the shared angel- root and by nearby words of heavenly goodness.
note.cn: 按共享的 angel- 词根与「神圣美好」的近义词分组。

entries.definition: relating to the Church of England
entries.definitionCN: 英国国教的，与 angelic 拼写相近但词源无关（出自拉丁 Anglicanus）

entries.definition: an angel of the highest rank
entries.definitionCN: 大天使，共享 angel- 词根

entries.definition: relating to the gospel, from Greek for good news
entries.definitionCN: 福音派的，同出希腊语「信使、消息」词根

entries.definition: relating to seraphim; blissfully pure
entries.definitionCN: 炽天使般的；极度纯洁的，与 angelic 义场相同

entries.definition: of heaven; wonderfully beautiful
entries.definitionCN: 天国的；极美的，日常近义表达

entries.definition: like a cherub, sweetly innocent in appearance
entries.definitionCN: 小天使般的；天真甜美的，多形容孩童面容

normalIntro.en: These hooks rest on the real Greek root angelos, messenger.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的希腊词根 angelos（信使）。

normal.en: angelos = Greek messenger; an angel is heaven's messenger, angelic describes that nature.
normal.cn: angelos 是希腊语「信使」；天使是天国的信使，angelic 形容其属性。

normal.en: Family: angel → angelic → angelically, one root growing wings.
normal.cn: 词族：angel → angelic → angelically，一个词根长出翅膀。

normal.en: Evangelical shares the messenger root: eu (good) + angelos (messenger) = good news.
normal.cn: evangelical 同出信使词根：eu（好）+ angelos（信使）= 好消息（福音）。

normal.en: Compare angelic wings with archangel's arch- (chief) prefix.
normal.cn: 比较 angelic 与 archangel 的 arch-（首领）前缀。

normal.en: Angelic patience and saintly patience describe the same rare virtue.
normal.cn: angelic patience 与 saintly patience 描述同一种难得的美德。

abstract.en: Picture soft white light around a sleeping child's face.
abstract.cn: 想象熟睡孩子面孔周围柔和的白光。

abstract.en: Hear a choir so clean it seems to come from above the ceiling.
abstract.cn: 聆听纯净得仿佛来自天花板之上的合唱。

abstract.en: Feel infinite patience, a smile that never tightens at the corners.
abstract.cn: 感受无限的耐心，一个嘴角永不僵硬的微笑。

examples.en: She sang with an angelic voice that silenced the hall.
examples.cn: 她的歌声如天籁般令全场安静。

examples.en: He endured the delay with angelic patience.
examples.cn: 他以天使般的耐心忍受了延误。

examples.en: The angelic child shared her sweets with everyone.
examples.cn: 那天使般的孩子把糖果分给了每个人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安洁丽可」——安静、洁白、美丽又可爱的天使，正是 angelic（天使般的）的画面。

root: 一般认为源自印欧词根 *her-（移动）→ 希腊语 angelos「信使」→ 拉丁语 angelus → 拉丁语 angelicus → 古法语 angelique → 英语 angelic。核心义为「天国信使（般）的」。

sensesIntro.en: From the messenger of heaven, the adjective spreads to faces, voices, kindness, patience, and even ironic masks of innocence.
sensesIntro.cn: 从天国信使出发，形容词铺展到面容、嗓音、善良、耐心，乃至带反讽的天真面具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glowing messenger of heaven
core.cn: 核心意象：散发柔光的天国信使

branches.en: innocence, real or worn as a mask

intro.en: The angel- family in English is mostly built with Greek and Latin suffixes on one stem.
intro.cn: 英语中的 angel- 词族主要是在单一词干上加希腊、拉丁后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin angelus supplied the stem that most English forms use.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 angelus 提供了多数英语词形所用的词干。

items.exampleCN: heroic 与 poetic 共用这一后缀。

items.example: A seraphic calm settled on her face.
items.exampleCN: 她脸上现出圣洁的平静。

items.example: Cherubic cheeks won the baby many admirers.
items.exampleCN: 婴儿胖嘟嘟的脸颊惹人怜爱。

items.example: Medieval angelology ranked nine choirs of angels.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪天使学将天使分为九个等级。

definition_zh: 角；角度；视角；斜向；钓鱼
definition_en: the space between two meeting lines, a way of looking at something, or to fish with a hook
core_image: 两条直线在顶点相交，形成一个张开的角
scene: 摄影师蹲下来，从很低的角度拍那栋楼，线条一下变得有力。She shot the building from a low angle.
sceneCN: 这里 angle 是「角度」（第 2 个义项：观察或拍摄的方向）；句意是她从低角度拍摄这栋楼。

pos.zh: 动词：斜向移动；钓鱼；谋求

derivatives.zh: 形容词：有角的；棱角分明的

senses.title: The space between lines
senses.definition: the figure formed where two lines or surfaces meet, measured in degrees
senses.definitionCN: 两条线或两个面相交处形成的图形，以度数计量
senses.example: The two walls meet at a right angle.
senses.exampleCN: 两面墙以直角相接。
senses.why: Latin angulus meant 'corner', so the geometric sense is the oldest: the word names the bend where two lines meet.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 angulus 意为「角、拐角」，所以几何义最古老：这个词指两条线相交处的那个弯。

senses.title: A point of view
senses.definition: a particular way of considering a situation or presenting a story
senses.definitionCN: 考虑问题或叙述事情的特定方式
senses.example: She shot the building from a low angle.
senses.exampleCN: 她从低角度拍摄了这栋楼。
senses.why: A corner gives a particular view of a room, so angle came to mean the position from which something is seen or judged.
senses.whyCN: 站在一个角落能看到房间的特定一面，所以 angle 引申为观察或判断事物的位置。

senses.title: To fish or to scheme
senses.definition: to fish with a hook, or to try to get something indirectly, as in angle for an invitation
senses.definitionCN: 用鱼钩钓鱼，或间接地谋求某物，如拐弯抹角地讨邀请
senses.example: They angled for trout in the cold stream.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在冰冷的溪流里钓鳟鱼。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different Old English word, angel, 'fishhook', which happened to merge in spelling with the geometric angle.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个古英语词 angel「鱼钩」，只是拼写恰好与几何义的 angle 合流。

intro.en: Angle is really two words in one coat: a Latin corner and an Old English fishhook.
intro.cn: angle 其实是两件外衣穿在一个词里：拉丁语的「角」与古英语的「鱼钩」。

items.en: angulus meant 'corner, bend', the source of the geometric sense.
items.cn: angulus 意为「角、弯」，是几何义的来源。

items.en: angel meant 'fishhook', a separate word that later shared the spelling angle.
items.cn: angel 意为「鱼钩」，是后来与 angle 共用拼写的另一个词。

items.en: French passed the Latin corner word into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 法语把拉丁语的「角」于十四世纪传入英语。

items.en: The fishing sense settled under the same spelling, and the verb to angle appeared.
items.cn: 钓鱼义在同一拼写下固定，动词 angle 也随之出现。

items.en: Modern English uses angle for geometry, viewpoint, and indirect seeking, while angler keeps the fishing link.
items.cn: 现代英语用 angle 表示几何角、视角与间接谋求，而 angler 保留钓鱼的联系。

note.en: The look-alike group warns about angel; the near-meaning group gives viewpoint words.
note.cn: 形近组提醒与 angel 的区别；近义组列视角类词。

abstract.cn: 想象摄影师蹲得很低。

abstract.en: Imagine a line cast into a cold stream.
abstract.cn: 想象鱼线抛进冰冷的溪水。

examples.cn: 画一条四十五度角的线。

examples.cn: 试着从另一个角度看这个问题。

examples.en: He angled for an invitation to the dinner.
examples.cn: 他拐弯抹角地想要一张晚宴请柬。

sensesIntro.en: A corner gives geometry and viewpoint; a fishhook gives the fishing and scheming sense.

definition_zh: 批评；非难；谴责性评论
definition_en: criticism or critical remark, especially a hostile or censorious comment
core_image: 目光转向、盯住过错：把心思转向别人的错处并说出口
scene: 评审会上，教授放下钢笔，皱起了眉。The committee's report contained a sharp animadversion on the mayor's spending.
sceneCN: 这里 animadversion 是「批评、非难」（第 1 个义项：指责性的评论）；句意为：委员会的报告对市长的开支提出了尖锐的批评。

derivatives.zh: animadversion 的动词形式，义为「批评；指责」
罕见派生，义为「批评性的；非难的」

senses.title: A critical or censorious remark
senses.definition: a comment that points out fault or expresses disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 指出过错或表达不满的评论
senses.example: The essay opened with an animadversion on modern architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 文章以对现代建筑的批评开篇。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to turn the mind toward something, here toward its faults.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词本义是「把心神转向某物」，此处转向的是其过错。

senses.title: Hostile criticism of a person
senses.definition: disapproving comment directed at a person or their conduct
senses.definitionCN: 针对某人或其行为的不满评论
senses.example: His animadversions on the general were repeated all over town.
senses.exampleCN: 他对将军的责难传遍了全城。
senses.why: Turning the mind toward a person often means fixing the gaze on their flaws.
senses.whyCN: 把心神转向一个人，往往意味着紧盯其缺点。

senses.title: Official or formal censure
senses.definition: formal expression of disapproval by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构正式表达的不满
senses.example: The senate's animadversions forced the official to resign.
senses.exampleCN: 元老院的谴责迫使该官员辞职。
senses.why: When institutions turn their attention to a fault, the result is censure.
senses.whyCN: 当机构将注意力转向过错，结果便是正式申斥。

senses.title: Notice or observation preceding judgment
senses.definition: observation or comment, not necessarily unfavorable (older sense)
senses.definitionCN: 观察或评论，未必含贬义（旧义）
senses.example: Early uses allowed animadversion to mean simple notice of a thing.
senses.exampleCN: 早期用法中 animadversion 可仅指对某事的注意。
senses.why: Before the hostile sense hardened, turning the mind toward a thing was neutral attention.
senses.whyCN: 在贬义固化之前，「把心神转向某物」只是中性的关注。

senses.title: Criticism in writing or print
senses.definition: written critical remarks, as in reviews or polemics
senses.definitionCN: 书面的批评言论，如评论或论战文字
senses.example: The pamphlet collected animadversions against the new tax law.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子汇集了针对新税法的批评。
senses.why: Critical remarks fixed in print multiply and travel, extending the word's reach.
senses.whyCN: 批评言论一经印行便传播开来，扩展了该词的使用范围。

senses.title: Judicial animadversion: a judge's rebuke
senses.definition: a rebuke delivered by a court or judge from the bench
senses.definitionCN: 法庭或法官当庭发出的训斥
senses.example: The judge's animadversion warned the lawyer against delay tactics.
senses.exampleCN: 法官的训诫警告该律师不得拖延。
senses.why: The bench turns its official gaze on misconduct and speaks it aloud.
senses.whyCN: 法庭将官方目光投向不当行为并公开说出，即为司法训诫。

senses.title: Criticism of ideas or works rather than persons
senses.definition: critical evaluation aimed at theories, texts, or works
senses.definitionCN: 针对理论、文本或作品的批评性评价
senses.example: Scholarly animadversion refined the theory over decades.
senses.exampleCN: 学界的批评使这一理论在数十年间不断完善。
senses.why: The turned gaze can rest on books as well as deeds.
senses.whyCN: 这「转过去的目光」既可落在行为上，也可落在书卷上。

senses.title: Animadversion to or upon: the act of animadverting
senses.definition: the action of animadverting, taking notice with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 进行批评、以不满态度加以指摘的行为
senses.example: His constant animadversion upon trivial matters wearied his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他不断对琐事加以指摘，令朋友们厌倦。
senses.why: Repeating the turned gaze turns criticism into a habit, and the noun names the habit itself.
senses.whyCN: 反复「转动的目光」使批评成为习惯，名词即指这种习惯性行为。

intro.en: Animadversion literally means a turning of the mind toward something; in English it settled into meaning the remarks made when that something is a fault.
intro.cn: animadversion 字面是「心神转向某物」；在英语中定型为当所转向者是过错时发出的评论，即批评。

items.en: The roots *h₂enh₁- (to breathe) underlie Latin animus, the mind or spirit.
items.cn: 一般认为印欧词根 *h₂enh₁-（呼吸）是拉丁语 animus（心神、精神）的来源。

items.en: Animadvertere joined animus (mind) and advertere (to turn toward), meaning to turn the mind to a thing, notice it, then censure it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 animadvertere 由 animus（心神）与 advertere（转向）构成，义为「将心神转向、注意到，进而责备」。

items.en: The noun animadversio named the noticing and the censure that followed.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 animadversio 指这种注意及随之而来的责备。

items.en: English took both verb and noun around 1600; at first the noun could mean simple observation.
items.cn: 英语约在 1600 年前后同时借入动词与名词；名词起初可仅指「注意、观察」。

items.en: The censorious sense prevailed, fixing animadversion as formal, often hostile criticism.
items.cn: 责难义逐渐占据主导，使 animadversion 定型为正式且常带敌意的批评。

entries.definition: a rare word for a turning toward
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的「转向」义词汇，是 animadversion 的直接构成成分之一

entries.definition: formal, severe disapproval
entries.definitionCN: 正式而严厉的责难

entries.definition: sharp criticism of a fault
entries.definitionCN: 尖锐的训斥，多针对具体过错

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real roots animus and advertere.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的词根 animus 与 advertere。

normal.en: animus = mind; ad = toward; vert = turn: turn your mind toward a fault and criticize it.
normal.cn: animus（心神）+ ad（朝向）+ vert（转）：把心神转向过错并加以批评。

normal.en: Same vert family: advert, avert, convert, all about turning.
normal.cn: 同属 vert 词族：advert、avert、convert，都与「转」有关。

normal.en: The verb animadvert matches the noun animadversion.
normal.cn: 动词 animadvert 与名词 animadversion 相对应。

normal.en: Animation keeps animus in its lively sense; animadversion turns it toward faults.
normal.cn: animation 保留 animus 的「生气」义；animadversion 则把心神转向过错。

normal.en: Formal writing prefers animadversion to casual criticism.
normal.cn: 正式文体更常用 animadversion 而非随口的 criticism。

abstract.en: Picture a head turning sharply toward one small error on a long page.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗头颅猛然转向长卷上的一处小错。

abstract.en: See an arrow of attention piercing one flaw in an otherwise fine report.
abstract.cn: 想象一支「注意力之箭」射中报告中唯一的瑕疵。

abstract.en: Feel the room go quiet when the censor's gaze lands.
abstract.cn: 感受审视的目光落下时全场骤然的安静。

examples.en: The review was full of animadversions on the director's earlier films.
examples.cn: 这篇评论满是对导演早期作品的批评。

examples.en: She escaped animadversion because her report was flawless.
examples.cn: 由于报告无懈可击，她免于受到批评。

examples.en: His animadversion upon the policy was quoted for weeks.
examples.cn: 他对该政策的非难被引用了数周。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺你骂我行」——你骂俺可以，俺骂你也行，互相 animadversion（批评、非难）。

sensesIntro.en: From turning the mind toward a thing, the word narrows into pointed criticism: of faults, persons, institutions, and texts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「心神转向某物」出发，词义收窄为指向分明的批评：过错、人物、机构与文本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the mind's gaze swiveling onto a fault
core.cn: 核心意象：心神的目光转向一处过错

branches.en: critical remarks on faults and works

branches.en: censure aimed at persons and officials

rebuke spoken from authority, habitually or not

intro.cn: animadversion 是拉丁双词根复合词：心神加转向。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语将 animus 与 advertere 复合，英语原样保留了这一结构。

items.example: Her animus against the plan was obvious.
items.exampleCN: 她对这一计划的敌意显而易见。

items.meaningCN: 气息；生命；心神（一般认为）
items.example: Animal and unanimous also carry this root.

items.exampleCN: 批评家就该小说的风格加以指摘。

items.example: Conversion and version share this noun ending.
items.exampleCN: conversion 与 version 共用这一名词词尾。

items.example: The house voted a censure on the minister.

latinEntries.meaning: to turn the mind to; to censure

derivatives.zh: 同源动词，义为「批评；指摘」

definition_zh: 批评；指责；非难
definition_en: to comment critically, to notice and censure a fault
core_image: 心神掉头盯住错处：目光一转，责备随之出口
scene: 编辑在稿纸上圈出一处错误。The senior editor animadverted on the sloppy citations in the draft.
sceneCN: 这里 animadvert 是「批评、指摘」（第 1 个义项：对过错加以指责性评论）；句意为：资深编辑对草稿中潦草的引注提出了批评。

pos.zh: 批评；指责（常与 on/upon 连用）

derivatives.zh: animadverting 的名词化，义为「批评；非难」

senses.title: To criticize a fault openly
senses.definition: to point out and censure a fault or shortcoming
senses.definitionCN: 指出并指责过错或缺点
senses.example: The reviewers animadverted on the careless proofreading.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者对粗心的校对提出了批评。
senses.why: The Latin sense of turning the mind toward a thing became fixing attention on its faults and saying so.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「把心神转向某物」之义演变为紧盯其过错并予以言明。

senses.title: To censure a person
senses.definition: to express disapproval of a person or their conduct
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或其行为表达不满
senses.example: The moralist animadverted upon the young poet's wild life.
senses.exampleCN: 这位道德家指摘年轻诗人放浪的生活。
senses.why: A gaze turned on a person usually lands on what deserves blame.
senses.whyCN: 转向一个人的目光，往往落在其应受责备之处。

senses.title: To take notice of something (older neutral sense)
senses.definition: to observe or take notice of a thing, without disapproval (earlier use)
senses.definitionCN: 观察或注意某事物，不带不满（早期用法）
senses.example: Early writers used the verb simply for noticing an event.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作者仅用该动词表示「注意到某事」。
senses.why: Before censure hardened in, turning the mind toward was mere attention.
senses.whyCN: 在责难义固化之前，「心神转向」只是单纯的注意。

senses.title: To pass judgment in an official capacity
senses.definition: to censure in an official or formal capacity
senses.definitionCN: 以官方或正式身份加以责备
senses.example: The court animadverted on the witness's evasive answers.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭就证人闪躲的回答予以训诫。
senses.why: When an authority's attention turns to misconduct, its words carry official weight.
senses.whyCN: 当权威的注意力转向不当行为，其言辞便带有官方分量。

senses.title: To animadvert against: to attack in words
senses.definition: to attack with critical words rather than actions
senses.definitionCN: 以批评性言辞而非行动加以攻击
senses.example: Pamphleteers animadverted against the new doctrine for years.
senses.exampleCN: 小册子作者们多年来抨击这一新学说。
senses.why: The turned gaze sharpens into a verbal weapon.
senses.whyCN: 转动的目光锐化为言辞的武器。

senses.title: To animadvert at length: to dwell on faults
senses.definition: to criticize repeatedly or at great length
senses.definitionCN: 反复或长篇地加以批评
senses.example: He animadverted at length on every detail of the menu.
senses.exampleCN: 他对菜单的每个细节都数落了一番。
senses.why: Dwelling attention, once fixed on faults, keeps returning to them.
senses.whyCN: 注意力一旦固定在过错上，便会反复回到其上。

senses.title: To criticise a work or doctrine
senses.definition: to evaluate critically a text, theory, or doctrine
senses.definitionCN: 对文本、理论或学说作批评性评价
senses.example: Philosophers animadverted on the new definition of knowledge.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家们对知识的新定义提出批评。
senses.why: Books as well as deeds can receive the turned gaze.
senses.whyCN: 书卷与行为同样能承受这「转来的目光」。

senses.title: To remark with implied disapproval
senses.titleCN: 委婉批评；暗含不满的评说
senses.definition: to comment in a way that carries implied criticism
senses.definitionCN: 以暗含批评的方式评论
senses.example: She animadverted gently on his habit of arriving late.
senses.exampleCN: 她委婉地批评了他迟到的习惯。
senses.why: Even a soft gaze turned toward a fault still points at it.
senses.whyCN: 即便是柔和的目光，一旦转向过错，仍然指向它。

intro.en: Animadvert is the verb behind animadversion, a Latin compound of mind plus turning that arrived in learned English around 1600.
intro.cn: animadvert 是 animadversion 的动词形式，为「心神 + 转向」的拉丁复合词，约 1600 年进入学术化英语。

items.en: The root *h₂enh₁- (to breathe) is generally taken to underlie Latin animus, mind or spirit.
items.cn: 一般认为印欧词根 *h₂enh₁-（呼吸）是拉丁语 animus（心神）的来源。

items.en: Animadvertere combined animus (mind) and advertere (to turn toward): to direct the mind at something.
items.cn: 拉丁语 animadvertere 由 animus（心神）与 advertere（转向）构成：将心神指向某物。

items.en: Classical usage added the step from noticing to censuring; Cicero used it of attending to a fault.
items.cn: 古典用法进一步由「注意」跨到「责备」；西塞罗即用它表示注意到过错。

items.en: English adopted the verb around 1600, first in the neutral sense of observing, soon in the hostile sense.
items.cn: 英语约 1600 年借入该动词，先是中性「注意」义，随后转为「指责」义。

items.en: Today it is a formal, bookish verb, almost always paired with on or upon.
items.cn: 如今它是正式而书卷气的动词，几乎总与 on 或 upon 搭配。

abstract.en: Picture an eye swiveling in its socket toward one red typo.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗眼球在眼眶中转向一个红色错字。

abstract.en: See a teacher's finger tapping one wrong line for a full minute.
abstract.cn: 想象老师的手指在错行上敲点整整一分钟。

abstract.en: Feel attention snap shut on a fault like a trap.
abstract.cn: 感受注意力如捕兽夹般「咔哒」锁住过错。

examples.en: The professor animadverted on several weak arguments in the thesis.
examples.cn: 教授批评了论文中几处薄弱的论证。

examples.en: Early critics animadverted upon what they saw as vanity in his verse.

examples.en: The court animadverted on the repeated delays.

senses.title: Strong hostility toward someone
senses.definition: a feeling of strong dislike and active ill will toward a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某群体的强烈厌恶与敌对情绪
senses.example: Years of rivalry turned into open animosity.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的较量演变为公开的敌意。
senses.why: The root spirit or breath became spirit roused against another spirit.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义「气息、精神」引申为「被激起而与对方作对的精神」。

senses.title: Bitter resentment kept alive over time
senses.definition: hostility that persists and festers over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期持续、不断发酵的敌对情绪
senses.example: The animosity between the rivals outlived their careers.
senses.exampleCN: 两位对手之间的积怨在退役后仍未消散。
senses.why: Spirit, once stirred against another, keeps breathing on its own.
senses.whyCN: 精神一旦被激起与对方作对，便会自行延续，如气息不熄。

senses.title: Ill will behind actions
senses.definition: hostile intention visible in what one does or says
senses.definitionCN: 从言行中透露出的敌对意图
senses.example: There was more animosity than logic in his objection.
senses.exampleCN: 他的反对里恶意多于道理。
senses.why: Inner spirit shows itself in outward acts, so the word names the motive force.
senses.whyCN: 内在精神会显露于外在行为，此词便指这种动机力量。

senses.title: Animosity between groups
senses.definition: hostility dividing communities, factions, or nations
senses.definitionCN: 使社区、派系或国家相互对立的敌意
senses.example: Border wars left a residue of animosity between the two nations.
senses.exampleCN: 边境战争在两国间留下仇视的余绪。
senses.why: What begins between persons scales up to whole peoples.
senses.whyCN: 始于个人的敌意可放大到整个民族。

senses.title: Open expression of hatred
senses.definition: hostility openly shown rather than hidden
senses.definitionCN: 公开表露而非隐藏的敌意
senses.example: She made no attempt to hide her animosity at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她毫不掩饰会上的敌意。
senses.why: Breath becomes speech; stirred spirit speaks out.
senses.whyCN: 气息化为言语，被激起的精神自会出口。

senses.title: Animosity in public life
senses.definition: hostility in politics, sports, or professional rivalries
senses.definitionCN: 政治、体育或职业竞争中的敌对
senses.example: The election season was marked by unusual animosity.
senses.exampleCN: 这次选举季充满罕见的敌对气氛。
senses.why: Contests for shared prizes breed stirred spirits on all sides.
senses.whyCN: 对共同奖赏的争夺使各方精神都被激起。

senses.title: Animosity as feeling versus action
senses.definition: the inner feeling itself, whether or not it leads to deeds
senses.definitionCN: 内心情绪本身，无论是否付诸行动
senses.example: He felt animosity but spoke with perfect courtesy.
senses.exampleCN: 他心怀敌意，言谈却彬彬有礼。
senses.why: Spirit exists inside the chest before it reaches the hands.
senses.whyCN: 精神在抵达双手之前，先在胸腔里存在。

senses.title: Deadly animosity: enmity to the extreme
senses.definition: hatred intense enough to admit no reconciliation
senses.definitionCN: 强烈到无法和解的仇恨
senses.example: The feud ended in deadly animosity between the houses.
senses.exampleCN: 这场世仇以两族间不共戴天的敌意收场。
senses.why: When stirred spirit refuses to settle, hostility becomes absolute.
senses.whyCN: 被激起的精神拒绝平息，敌意便走向绝对化。

intro.en: Animosity shares its breathing root with animal and animate: it is spirit roused against another.
intro.cn: animosity 与 animal、animate 共享「气息」词根：它是被激起而与人对立的精神。

items.en: The root *h₂enh₁- meant to breathe, giving Latin animus, breath, spirit, and mind.
items.cn: 印欧词根 *h₂enh₁- 义为「呼吸」，派生出拉丁语 animus（气息、精神、心神）。

items.en: Animositas meant boldness and high spirit, later violent feeling against someone.
items.cn: 拉丁语 animositas 意为「大胆、气盛」，后指针对他人的激烈情绪。

items.en: Old French carried animosite, keeping the sense of violent feeling.
items.cn: 古法语作 animosite，保留「激烈情绪」之义。

items.en: English adopted animosity in the fifteenth century, at first meaning courage or vigor.
items.cn: 英语于十五世纪借入 animosity，最初意为「勇气、活力」。

items.en: The hostile sense prevailed by the seventeenth century, fixing the modern meaning of hatred and ill will.
items.cn: 至十七世纪敌对义占上风，确立了现代「仇恨、敌意」之义。

normal.en: anim- = breath, spirit; animosity is spirit stirred up against someone.
normal.cn: anim- 表「气息、精神」；animosity 是被激起而针对他人的精神。

normal.en: Same root: animal (breathing thing), animate (give breath to), unanimous (one spirit).
normal.cn: 同根词：animal（有气息之物）、animate（赋予气息）、unanimous（同一心神）。

normal.en: Animus names the hostile intent; animosity the hostile feeling.
normal.cn: animus 指敌对意图；animosity 指敌对情绪。

normal.en: Unanimous is the opposite mood: many people, one spirit, no animosity.
normal.cn: unanimous 恰是相反氛围：众人心神一致，毫无敌意。

normal.en: Collocation memory: bear animosity toward someone.
normal.cn: 搭配记忆：bear animosity toward someone（对某人怀有敌意）。

abstract.en: Picture a black wind swirling inside the chest every time a rival's name is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象每当听到对手的名字，胸腔里便卷起黑风。

abstract.en: See two old neighbors never greeting each other across the fence for decades.
abstract.cn: 想象两位老邻居隔着篱笆几十年互不寒暄。

abstract.en: Feel the heat rising in the face before a single harsh word is said.
abstract.cn: 感受一句重话未出口前脸上先升起的燥热。

examples.en: Despite the animosity between them, they worked together for ten years.
examples.cn: 尽管彼此有敌意，他们还是共事了十年。

examples.en: The animosity between the two clubs goes back a century.
examples.cn: 两家俱乐部之间的宿怨可追溯到一个世纪前。

examples.en: He bore no animosity toward his former partner.
examples.cn: 他对前合伙人毫无敌意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱你莫提」——都到「爱你」都不敢提的地步了，只剩 animosity（敌意）。

root: 拉丁语 animus（气息、心神，源自一般认为的印欧词根 *h₂enh₁-「呼吸」）+ -ositas（名词后缀）→ animositas「气盛；激烈情绪」→ 古法语 animosite → 英语 animosity（15 世纪，最初义为「勇气」，17 世纪转为「敌意」）。

sensesIntro.en: From roused spirit, the word fans out into personal hatred, long-fed grudges, group hostility, and hatred expressed or merely felt.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「被激起的精神」出发，词义铺展为个人仇恨、经年积怨、群体敌对，以及表露于外或仅存于心的恨意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black wind of spirit blowing against someone
core.cn: 核心意象：吹向他人的黑色精神之风

branches.cn: 随时间加深的积怨与死仇

branches.en: ill will behind words and deeds
hostility between groups and in public life
branches.cn: 群体间与公共领域的敌对

intro.en: The anim- family is one of Latin's largest: breath becomes life, mind, courage, and here hostility.
intro.cn: anim- 词族是拉丁语最庞大的词族之一：气息化为生命、心神、勇气，在此则化为敌意。

latinIntro.en: Latin animus supplied all members of the family, each suffix tilting the meaning its own way.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 animus 供应该词族所有成员，不同后缀使词义各自偏移。

items.example: Every anim- word starts from breathing.
items.exampleCN: 每个 anim- 词都始于「呼吸」。

items.example: Curiosity and generosity share this ending.
items.exampleCN: curiosity 与 generosity 共用此词尾。

items.example: Animal once meant simply anything alive.
The coach animated the tired team.
items.exampleCN: 教练使疲惫的队伍重燃斗志。

items.example: The vote was unanimous.
She spoke without animus.
A magnanimous winner praised the loser.
items.exampleCN: 获胜者宽宏地称赞了败者。

items.example: A pusillanimous retreat avoided the battle.
items.exampleCN: 怯懦的撤退避开了战斗。

derivatives.zh: animosity 的复数形式，指多股敌意

definition_zh: 编年史；年鉴；历史记载
definition_en: historical records arranged year by year; a written account of events
core_image: 一页页按年份排好的流水账：去年在前，今年在后
scene: 档案馆里，管理员翻开厚厚的册子。The monastery's annals record every flood and harvest since the twelfth century.
sceneCN: 这里 annals 是「编年史」（第 1 个义项：逐年记录的历史文献）；句意为：修道院的编年史记录了十二世纪以来的每场洪水和每次收成。

pos.zh: 编年史；年记载（常用复数）

derivatives.zh: annals 的书写者，义为「编年史家」

senses.title: Year-by-year historical records
senses.definition: written records of events arranged in yearly order
senses.definitionCN: 按年份顺序编排的事件记录
senses.example: The monk kept the annals of the abbey until his death.
senses.exampleCN: 这位修士直到去世都在记录修道院的编年史。
senses.why: The Latin annalis means yearly, so the word names records organized year by year.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 annalis 意为「每年的」，故该词指逐年编排的记录。

senses.title: Historical records in general
senses.definition: historical accounts and documents collectively
senses.definitionCN: 历史记述与文献的总称
senses.example: Her name appears in the annals of polar exploration.
senses.exampleCN: 她的名字出现在极地探险的史册中。
senses.why: Any dignified old record resembles the yearly chronicles, so the plural widened.
senses.whyCN: 任何庄重的旧文献都与逐年编录相似，复数词义因此扩宽。

senses.title: The annals of a field or activity
senses.definition: the recorded history of a profession, art, or science
senses.definitionCN: 某一职业、艺术或学科的有记载的历史
senses.example: It was the strangest trial in the annals of jurisprudence.
senses.exampleCN: 那是法学史册上最离奇的一场审判。
senses.why: Every discipline keeps its own chronicle of firsts and extremes.
senses.whyCN: 每个学科都保有属于自己的「首创与极致」编年。

senses.title: To go down in the annals: lasting fame
senses.definition: to be remembered permanently in history
senses.definitionCN: 被永久地记入历史
senses.example: The rescue went down in the annals of seamanship.
senses.exampleCN: 这次营救被载入航海史册。
senses.why: To enter the yearly book is to outlive one's own years.
senses.whyCN: 进入逐年之册，便超越了自身短暂的岁月。

senses.title: A journal or periodical title
senses.definition: the title of scholarly periodicals, as in Annals of Mathematics
senses.definitionCN: 学术期刊的题名，如《数学年刊》
senses.example: He published his proof in the Annals of Statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 他在《统计学年刊》上发表了证明。
senses.why: Learned societies borrowed the chronicler's word for their yearbooks of research.
senses.whyCN: 学术团体借用了编年史家之词来命名研究年鉴。

senses.title: Annals as dull minute record-keeping
senses.titleCN: 流水账式记录（略带贬义）
senses.definition: dry, itemized record without interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 不加解读、逐条罗列的干瘪记录
senses.example: The minutes read like bare annals, date after date.
senses.exampleCN: 会议纪要读来如同干巴巴的流水账，一个日期接一个日期。
senses.why: Chronicles list events without explaining them, inviting the pejorative shade.
senses.whyCN: 编年史只列事件不加解释，因而带上贬义色彩。

senses.title: The whole remembered past of a people
senses.definition: the entire recorded past of a nation or culture
senses.definitionCN: 一个民族或文化的全部有记载的过去
senses.example: War haunts the annals of that small country.
senses.exampleCN: 战争萦绕着那个小国的整部史册。
senses.why: Year after year, the annals accumulate into a people's whole memory.
senses.whyCN: 一年又一年，编年史累积为民族的整部记忆。

senses.title: In the annals of crime or scandal
senses.definition: the record of notable misdeeds
senses.definitionCN: 著名恶行或丑闻的记录
senses.example: The fraud ranks high in the annals of corporate crime.
senses.exampleCN: 这起欺诈在企业犯罪记录中名列前茅。
senses.why: The chronicle keeps both triumphs and disgraces on its pages.
senses.whyCN: 编年之册既录辉煌，也载耻辱。

intro.en: Annals is simply the plural of a Latin adjective meaning yearly, and it has never lost its calendar bones.
intro.cn: annals 本是一个意为「每年的」拉丁形容词的复数，其历法骨架从未丢失。

items.en: The root *at- meant to go, and through walking the circuit came to mean a year.
items.cn: 印欧词根 *at- 义为「行走」，经由「走完一圈」引申为「一年」。

items.en: Annus meant year; annalis was its adjective, yearly, applied to the pontiffs' yearly records.
items.cn: 拉丁语 annus 意为「年」，形容词 annalis 意为「每年的」，用于大祭司的逐年记录。

items.en: Annales became the name of the yearly priestly chronicles of Rome.
items.cn: Annales 成为罗马大祭司逐年编录史册的名称。

items.en: English borrowed the plural directly as annals in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪直接以复数形式借入 annals。

items.en: The word now covers chronicles, any dignified record, and the titles of learned journals.
items.cn: 如今该词既指编年史，也泛指庄重的记载与学术年刊之名。

note.en: The groups below split by shared year-roots and by neighboring record words.
note.cn: 以下按「同出年之词根」与「近义记录词」分组。

entries.definition: happening once a year
entries.definitionCN: 每年的，与 annals 同出 annus 词根

entries.definition: a yearly payment
entries.definitionCN: 年金，同根且同样按年计算

entries.definition: relating to the anus; (psychology) excessively orderly
entries.definitionCN: 肛门的；（心理）过分拘泥的，与 annals 只是拼写相近，词源无关

entries.definition: a factual written account in order of time
entries.definitionCN: 编年史；记事，与 annals 最近的近义词

entries.definition: collections of historical documents
entries.definitionCN: 档案；案卷，偏收藏而非逐年记录

entries.definition: documented accounts of past events
entries.definitionCN: 记录；史料，最泛化的表达

normalIntro.en: These hooks are built on the real Latin root annus, year.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的拉丁词根 annus（年）。

normal.en: annus = year; annals are records made year by year.
normal.cn: annus 表「年」；annals 即逐年写就的记录。

normal.en: Same root set: annual, anniversary, annuity, biennial.
normal.cn: 同根词组：annual、anniversary、annuity、biennial。

normal.en: Annals is almost always plural, like the many pages of a chronicle.
normal.cn: annals 几乎总是复数，如同编年史的众多页卷。

normal.en: The phrase go down in the annals of history fixes the sense in memory.
normal.cn: 「载入史册」的惯用短语可帮助固定词义。

normal.en: Annalist is the chronicler; annalistic describes the dry year-by-year style.
normal.cn: annalist 是编年史家；annalistic 形容逐年干记的风格。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of ledgers, one spine per decade, dust on the top edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一排账册式的史书，每十年一卷，顶边落着灰尘。

abstract.en: See a monk dipping his pen to write the single line for this year.
abstract.cn: 想象修士蘸笔为今年写下短短一行。

abstract.en: Feel the weight of centuries pressing into one closing book.
abstract.cn: 感受数百年光阴压进一部合上的史册。

examples.en: The battle earned its place in the annals of military history.
examples.cn: 这一战在军事史册上占据了一席之地。

examples.en: Local annals mention a great fire in 1687.
examples.cn: 地方编年史提到 1687 年的一场大火。

examples.en: It was, in the annals of sport, a performance without equal.
examples.cn: 在体育史册上，那是一场无与伦比的表演。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「年年记」——按年记录的历史，谐音联想「俺诺斯」每年都来记上一笔，正是 annals（编年史）。

root: 拉丁语 annus（年，源自一般认为的印欧词根 *at-「行走」，走完一循环即一年）→ 形容词 annalis「每年的」→ 罗马大祭司的逐年史册 Annales → 英语 annals（16 世纪，直接借入复数形式）。

sensesIntro.en: From yearly records the word stretches to any dignified record, a field's own history, the dry style of mere listing, and journal titles.
sensesIntro.cn: 从逐年记录出发，词义延伸至一切庄重记载、学科自身的历史、干瘪的罗列风格，以及学术年刊之名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger with one line per year
core.cn: 核心意象：每年一行的册页

branches.en: fame and disgrace preserved on the page
the dry style of mere listing
branches.cn: 干瘪罗列的流水账风格

intro.en: The ann- year family in English is compact and highly regular.
intro.cn: 英语中的 ann- 「年」词族紧凑而规整。

latinIntro.en: Latin annus generates most of the family through adjective and noun suffixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 annus 通过形容词、名词后缀衍生出该词族的大部分成员。

items.example: Per annum means by the year.

items.meaningCN: 年；走完的一圈（一般认为）
items.example: The ring of ann- words all count time in years.
items.exampleCN: ann- 词族都以「年」计时间。

items.example: Annual means yearly in occurrence.
An annalist writes the annals.
Interest is charged at five percent per annum.
items.exampleCN: 利息按年利率百分之五计收。

items.example: The biennial exhibition attracts collectors.
items.exampleCN: 两年一度的展览吸引收藏家。

items.example: A perennial favorite returns each season.
items.exampleCN: 那道常青的保留节目每季回归。

items.example: Annals may span several centuries.
items.exampleCN: 编年史可跨越数个世纪。

derivatives.zh: annals + -istic，义为「编年史式的；逐条罗列的」

definition_zh: 彻底消灭；歼灭；使完全失效
definition_en: to destroy utterly; to reduce to nothing
core_image: 把东西化成零：不但打碎，连渣都不留
scene: 棋局终了，棋手推倒了对方的王。A sudden cavalry charge annihilated the enemy's left wing.
sceneCN: 这里 annihilate 是「歼灭」（第 1 个义项：彻底摧毁）；句意为：一次骑兵冲锋彻底歼灭了敌人的左翼。

derivatives.zh: annihilate 的名词形式，义为「毁灭；歼灭」

senses.title: To destroy completely
senses.definition: to destroy something or someone entirely, leaving nothing effective behind
senses.definitionCN: 将某人某物彻底摧毁，不留任何有生力量
senses.example: The hurricane annihilated the coastal villages.
senses.exampleCN: 飓风彻底摧毁了沿海村庄。
senses.why: The Latin phrase meant to reduce to nothing, so any total destruction fits.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语短语本义是「化为无」，因此一切彻底摧毁都适用。

senses.title: To defeat overwhelmingly
senses.definition: to defeat an opponent by an overwhelming margin
senses.definitionCN: 以压倒性优势击败对手
senses.example: The champions annihilated the newcomers ten to nil.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军队以十比零横扫新军。
senses.why: Defeat so complete that the loser counts as nothing borrows the language of destruction.
senses.whyCN: 败到近乎「不存在」的失利，借用了毁灭的语言。

senses.title: To void or nullify in law
senses.definition: to cancel the legal force of something completely
senses.definitionCN: 完全取消某物的法律效力
senses.example: The court annihilated the fraudulent contract.
senses.exampleCN: 法院使这份欺诈合同完全失效。
senses.why: A thing rendered legally nothing is as good as destroyed.
senses.whyCN: 法律上化为乌有之物，等同于被摧毁。

senses.title: Matter-antimatter annihilation in physics
senses.definition: the conversion of a particle and its antiparticle into energy
senses.definitionCN: 粒子与反粒子相互转化并释放能量的过程
senses.example: When matter meets antimatter, both annihilate into gamma rays.
senses.exampleCN: 物质与反物质相遇时湮灭为伽马射线。
senses.why: Physics gives the old word a precise meaning: mass truly reduced to energy, to nothing left.
senses.whyCN: 物理学赋予旧词精确含义：质量真正化为能量，不留残余。

senses.title: To crush hopes or arguments
senses.definition: to destroy hopes, arguments, or morale utterly
senses.definitionCN: 彻底粉碎希望、论点或士气
senses.example: One question from the bench annihilated his argument.
senses.exampleCN: 法官席上的一个问题就粉碎了他的论点。
senses.why: Invisible things too can be reduced to nothing.
senses.whyCN: 无形之物同样可以被化为乌有。

senses.title: To annihilate distance or obstacles
senses.definition: to remove an obstacle so completely it seems not to exist
senses.definitionCN: 将障碍消除到仿佛不存在
senses.example: The telegraph annihilated distance across the continent.
senses.exampleCN: 电报消除了横跨大陆的距离。
senses.why: That which no longer hinders is as if annihilated.
senses.whyCN: 不再构成阻碍之物，视同被消灭。

senses.title: To self-annihilate in mysticism
senses.definition: to extinguish the self utterly before the divine
senses.definitionCN: 在神圣面前彻底消解自我
senses.example: The mystics spoke of annihilating the self in God.
senses.exampleCN: 神秘主义者谈在上帝之中消融自我。
senses.why: If a thing must become nothing to be perfected, annihilation turns devotional.
senses.whyCN: 若物须化为无方能成全，毁灭便转为虔修之义。

senses.title: To annihilate in nuclear strategy
senses.definition: to inflict destruction of a scale that ends a state's existence
senses.definitionCN: 造成足以终结一个国家存在的毁灭规模
senses.example: Deterrence rested on the threat of mutual annihilation.
senses.exampleCN: 威慑建立在对相互毁灭的威胁之上。
senses.why: Total destruction scaled up from armies to whole societies.
senses.whyCN: 彻底毁灭的尺度从军队扩大到整个社会。

intro.en: Annihilate says its own recipe in Latin: ad plus nihil plus a verb ending, to make into nothing.
intro.cn: annihilate 在拉丁语里写明了自己的配方：ad + nihil + 动词词尾，「化为无」。

items.en: The root *neh₂- meant not, and its negative force survives in nihil.
items.cn: 印欧词根 *neh₂- 义为「不」，其否定力量保留在 nihil 之中。

items.en: Nihil meant nothing, a contraction of nihilum; annihilare meant to reduce to nothing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nihil 意为「无」，是 nihilum 的紧缩形式；annihilare 义为「化为无」。

items.en: Annihilatio named the act of reducing a thing to nothing.
items.cn: 后拉丁语 annihilatio 指将某物化为无的行为。

items.en: English adopted annihilate in the fifteenth century, first in theological and legal contexts.
items.cn: 英语于十五世纪借入 annihilate，最初用于神学与法律语境。

items.en: Physics, war, and sport have since extended the word, while its core of utter nothingness stays intact.
items.cn: 此后物理、战争与体育不断扩展其用法，而「化为乌有」的核心义始终未变。

note.en: Grouped by the shared nihil root and by neighboring destruction words.
note.cn: 按共享的 nihil 词根与毁灭类近义词分组。

entries.definition: the act of annihilating
entries.definitionCN: 毁灭；歼灭，annihilate 的名词形式，同根

entries.definition: the belief that life and values are meaningless
entries.definitionCN: 虚无主义，共享 nihil（无）词根

entries.definition: a yearly payment
entries.definitionCN: 年金，与 annihilate 开头拼写相近但词根无关（annus 年）

entries.definition: to erase all traces of
entries.definitionCN: 抹去一切痕迹，强调「不留痕迹」

entries.definition: to destroy a whole group, especially pests or peoples
entries.definitionCN: 灭绝（多指害虫或族群）

entries.definition: to lay waste; to shock deeply
entries.definitionCN: 蹂躏；（情感上）重创，程度相近但留有残迹

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin compound ad + nihil.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的拉丁复合词 ad + nihil。

normal.en: ad (to) + nihil (nothing) = to nothing: annihilate means reduce to nothing.
normal.cn: ad（朝向）+ nihil（无）= 化为无：annihilate 即「消灭殆尽」。

normal.en: Same nihil family: nihilism, nihil obstat.
normal.cn: 同属 nihil 词族：nihilism、nihil obstat。

normal.en: The noun annihilation is standard in physics talk of matter and antimatter.
normal.cn: 名词 annihilation 是物理学谈论正反物质的常用词。

normal.en: Note the double n at the start, from ad + nihil fusing.
normal.cn: 注意开头的双 n，来自 ad + nihil 的融合。

normal.en: Sports headlines love annihilate for crushing victories.
normal.cn: 体育标题爱用 annihilate 描述碾压式胜利。

abstract.en: Picture a sandcastle erased so cleanly the beach looks untouched.
abstract.cn: 想象沙堡被抹得干干净净，沙滩仿佛从未被动过。

abstract.en: See two sparks, matter and antimatter, vanish in one flash of light.
abstract.cn: 想象物质与反物质两点火花在闪光中同时消失。

abstract.en: Feel a scoreboard reading ten to zero telling the whole story.
abstract.cn: 感受十比零的记分牌讲述的一切。

examples.en: The fire annihilated the old warehouse district.

examples.en: The home team annihilated the visitors in the second half.

examples.en: His cross-examination annihilated the witness's story.
examples.cn: 他的盘问彻底击垮了证人的说辞。

definition_zh: 毁灭；歼灭；湮灭；彻底失败
definition_en: the act of destroying something completely, or total destruction itself
core_image: 归零的瞬间：一切存在被抹为无
scene: 战报送到指挥部，地图上一支箭头消失了。The general's gamble ended in the annihilation of his entire army.
sceneCN: 这里 annihilation 是「歼灭、彻底毁灭」（第 1 个义项：完全摧毁的行为或结果）；句意为：将军的豪赌以全军覆没告终。
