senses.title: Complete destruction in war
senses.definition: the total destruction of an army, city, or people in conflict
senses.definitionCN: 战争中军队、城市或族群被彻底摧毁
senses.example: The campaign ended in the annihilation of the invading force.
senses.exampleCN: 这场战役以入侵部队全军覆没告终。
senses.why: The Latin root means to reduce to nothing, and war provides the most literal reduction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根义为「化为无」，战争提供了最字面意义上的归零。

senses.title: Utter defeat in competition
senses.definition: an overwhelming defeat in a game or contest
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或竞争中一边倒的惨败
senses.example: Fans still talk about the annihilation of the visitors in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 球迷仍在谈论决赛中客队的一败涂地。
senses.why: A defeat so total that the loser vanishes from the scoreboard borrows the language of ruin.
senses.whyCN: 败得从记分牌上「消失」的失利，借用了毁灭的语言。

senses.title: Particle-antiparticle annihilation in physics
senses.definition: the process in which a particle and its antiparticle convert into energy
senses.definitionCN: 粒子与反粒子相互转化并释放能量的物理过程
senses.example: Electron-positron annihilation produces two gamma photons.
senses.exampleCN: 正负电子湮灭产生两个伽马光子。
senses.why: Physics makes the metaphor exact: mass truly becomes nothing but energy.
senses.whyCN: 物理学使比喻成为精确事实：质量真的只化为能量，别无余留。

senses.title: Threat to the existence of a state or group
senses.definition: destruction so complete that a nation or group ceases to exist
senses.definitionCN: 使国家或族群不复存在的彻底毁灭
senses.example: Nuclear weapons raised the specter of mutual annihilation.
senses.exampleCN: 核武器带来了相互毁灭的幽灵。
senses.why: When destruction extends past armies to whole societies, the stakes become existence itself.
senses.whyCN: 当毁灭的范围越过军队扩及整个社会，赌注便成为存在本身。

senses.title: Annihilation of hope, morale, or arguments
senses.definition: the complete destruction of intangible things such as hopes or theories
senses.definitionCN: 希望、理论等无形之物的彻底破灭
senses.example: The scandal meant the annihilation of his political hopes.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻意味着他政治希望的彻底破灭。
senses.why: Anything that can be built can be reduced to nothing, including what has no atoms.
senses.whyCN: 凡能建立之物皆可归于无，包括没有原子的东西。

senses.title: Annihilation of distance or barriers
senses.definition: the complete removal of separation or hindrance
senses.definitionCN: 阻隔或障碍的彻底消除
senses.example: Air travel brought the annihilation of distance between continents.
senses.exampleCN: 航空旅行消除了大陆之间的距离阻隔。
senses.why: What no longer hinders at all may be said to have been annihilated.
senses.whyCN: 完全不再构成阻碍之物，可视为已被「消灭」。

senses.title: Self-annihilation in religion or mysticism
senses.definition: the mystical extinction of the individual self before the divine
senses.definitionCN: 在神圣面前个体自我的消解
senses.example: Sufi poetry describes annihilation of the self in divine love.
senses.exampleCN: 苏菲诗歌描述在神圣之爱中消融自我。
senses.why: Becoming nothing is here not a loss but the highest union.
senses.whyCN: 化为无在此并非损失，而是最高的合一。

senses.title: Annihilation in ecology or history
senses.definition: the wiping out of species, cultures, or ways of life
senses.definitionCN: 物种、文化或生活方式的消灭
senses.example: The annihilation of the buffalo herds changed the plains forever.
senses.exampleCN: 野牛群的灭绝永远改变了这片平原。
senses.why: Whole living worlds can be reduced to nothing by human hands.
senses.whyCN: 整个人类世界可能因人之手而化为无。

intro.en: Annihilation is the noun of annihilate, keeping the Latin recipe of making into nothing on its label.
intro.cn: annihilation 是 annihilate 的名词形式，标签上仍写着拉丁配方「化为无」。

items.en: The negative root *neh₂- (not) lies behind Latin nihil, nothing.
items.cn: 否定词根 *neh₂-（不）是拉丁语 nihil（无）的来源，属一般认为的重构。

items.en: Nihil or nihilum meant nothing; the verb annihilare meant to bring a thing to nothing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nihil 或 nihilum 意为「无」；动词 annihilare 意为「使物化为无」。

items.en: Annihilatio named the completed act of reducing to nothing.
items.cn: 后拉丁语 annihilatio 指已完成的「化为无」行为。

items.en: The noun entered English with annihilate, first in theological talk of the soul's annihilation.
items.cn: 名词与动词一同进入英语，最初用于神学中「灵魂归于无」的讨论。

items.en: War, physics, sport, and ecology have each claimed the word, all keeping its core of totality.
items.cn: 战争、物理、体育与生态学各自使用该词，而「彻底」的核心义不变。

note.en: Grouped by shared nihil roots and by words nearby in the field of total destruction.
note.cn: 按共享 nihil 词根与「彻底毁灭」义场的近义词分组。

abstract.en: Picture a galaxy of sand grains blown flat, the desert smooth again.
abstract.cn: 想象一把细沙被吹平，沙漠恢复平整。

abstract.en: See two photons leave where a particle used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象粒子消失之处射出两枚光子。

abstract.en: Feel a name being crossed off every list it ever appeared on.
abstract.cn: 感受一个名字从所有名单上被划去。

examples.cn: 这座城市从未从 1945 年的毁灭中恢复。

examples.cn: 科学家观测到粒子束之间的湮灭。

examples.en: The final was an annihilation, six goals to none.
examples.cn: 那场决赛是一场碾压，六比零。

definition_zh: 注释；作注解；评注
definition_en: to add explanatory notes to a text or diagram
core_image: 在书页边缘写下小字：为正文点灯
scene: 图书馆里，研究生在旧书页边写下小字。Students annotate their textbooks with questions and explanations.
sceneCN: 这里 annotate 是「注释」（第 1 个义项：为文本添加说明性批注）；句意为：学生们在教科书上写下问题和解释作为批注。

derivatives.zh: annotate 的名词形式，义为「注释；批注」
annotate 的过去分词形容词，义为「有注释的」

senses.title: To add explanatory notes to a text
senses.definition: to add notes that explain or comment on a written work
senses.definitionCN: 为书面作品添加解释性或评论性批注
senses.example: The editor annotated the letter with dates and names.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑为信件添加了日期与人名的注释。
senses.why: The Latin notare means to mark, and a note is a mark made beside the text.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 notare 意为「作标记」，note 即写在正文之旁的标记。

senses.title: To supply critical commentary
senses.definition: to add notes that judge or interpret, not merely explain
senses.definitionCN: 添加具评判或阐释性质而非仅说明的批注
senses.example: Scholars annotated the poem with competing interpretations.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们以相互竞争的解读为这首诗作评注。
senses.why: Marks beside a text grow from glosses into arguments.
senses.whyCN: 写在旁边的标记从「释义」成长为「论辩」。

senses.title: To label a diagram or dataset
senses.definition: to add labels or descriptions to images, maps, or data
senses.definitionCN: 为图像、地图或数据添加标签或说明
senses.example: The team annotated the X-rays before the review.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在会诊前为 X 光片加了标注。
senses.why: The page expands to any surface where marks explain content.
senses.whyCN: 「页面」扩展到一切可加注说明的表面。

senses.title: To mark up for a machine (computing)
senses.definition: to tag data with labels for training or analysis
senses.definitionCN: 为训练或分析给数据打标签
senses.example: Volunteers annotated thousands of street photos.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者为数千张街景照片做了标注。
senses.why: The old marginal mark becomes a digital label.
senses.whyCN: 古老的页边标记变成了数字标签。

senses.title: To furnish a text with apparatus
senses.definition: to prepare a scholarly edition with notes, sources, and cross-references
senses.definitionCN: 编订附有注释、出处与互见的学术版本
senses.example: She spent a decade annotating the medieval manuscript.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了十年为这部中世纪手稿作注。
senses.why: Notes accumulate into a whole scholarly apparatus around the old text.
senses.whyCN: 注释累积为围绕古文本的整套学术 apparatus。

senses.title: To annotate on or upon: to comment at large
senses.definition: to comment on or discuss a subject at length (older use)
senses.definitionCN: 对某题作长篇评论（旧式用法）
senses.example: Early writers annotated on the classics at book length.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作家以整本书的篇幅评述经典。
senses.why: When notes are spoken aloud, they become commentary.
senses.whyCN: 当注释被大声说出，便成为评论。

senses.title: To record observations alongside events
senses.definition: to add running notes to a log, timeline, or record
senses.definitionCN: 在日志、时间线或记录旁添加随行批注
senses.example: The pilot annotated the flight log with weather remarks.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员在飞行日志上添加了天气备注。
senses.why: Every official record admits marginal remarks from experience.
senses.whyCN: 一切正式记录都容纳来自经验的页边备注。

senses.title: To annotate oneself: to be marked by traces
senses.definition: to bear marks or traces that need explaining
senses.definitionCN: 带有需要解释的痕迹或标记
senses.example: The map annotated itself with every route the caravan took.
senses.exampleCN: 商队走过的每条路线都在地图上留下了标记。
senses.why: The direction of noting can reverse: the world marks us back.
senses.whyCN: 「作注」的方向可以反转：世界也会反过来标记我们。

intro.en: Annotate is built openly from Latin parts: to note upon, to make a mark against a text.
intro.cn: annotate 由拉丁部件透明构成：在文本之上作标记，即「加注」。

items.en: The root *ǵneh₃- meant to know, the same root that gives know and cognition.
items.cn: 印欧词根 *ǵneh₃- 意为「知道」，与 know、cognition 同根，一般认为。

items.en: Noscere meant to know; notare meant to mark, from nota, a mark or sign.
items.cn: 拉丁语 noscere 意为「知道」；notare 意为「作标记」，出自 nota（标记、符号）。

items.en: Adnotare combined ad (to) and notare, meaning to note down about a thing.
items.cn: 后拉丁语 adnotare 由 ad（对）加 notare 构成，义为「就某事作记录」。

items.en: English adopted annotate in the early seventeenth century for scholarly glossing.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪初借入 annotate，用于学术注释。

items.en: The verb now spans manuscripts, diagrams, logs, and machine-learning datasets.
items.cn: 如今该动词覆盖手稿、图表、日志与机器学习数据集。

definition_zh: 每年的；一年一次的；全年的；年刊
definition_en: happening once every year, calculated over a period of one year, or a book published once a year
core_image: 桌上摊开的一叠年度报表
scene: 年终大会上，财务把一叠报表放在桌上。The company publishes an annual report every spring.
sceneCN: 这里 annual 是「年度的」（第 2 个义项：按一整年计算或覆盖一整年）；句意是公司每年春天发布年度报告。

senses.title: Happening once a year
senses.definition: happening, done, or produced once every year
senses.definitionCN: 每年发生、进行或产出一次的
senses.example: The village holds an annual fair in September.
senses.exampleCN: 村里每年九月举办一次集市。
senses.why: Annual is the adjective from Latin annus, 'year', so it marks the thing that comes round once in that cycle.
senses.whyCN: annual 是拉丁语 annus「年」的形容词，因此用来标示在那个周期里出现一次的事物。

senses.title: Calculated over a year
senses.definition: measured over or covering a full year, as with income, leave, or growth
senses.definitionCN: 按整年计算或涵盖整年的，如收入、假期或增长率
senses.example: The company publishes an annual report every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 公司每年春天发布年度报告。
senses.why: The year is also a unit of measurement, so annual can mean the total for one year rather than an event inside it.
senses.whyCN: 年也可以是一个计量单位，所以 annual 能表示一整年的总额，而不是一年中发生的某件事。

senses.title: A yearly publication
senses.definition: a book, magazine, or collection published once a year
senses.definitionCN: 每年出版一次的书籍、杂志或作品集
senses.example: She bought the school annual as a souvenir.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了学校年刊留作纪念。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective of time into a noun for the thing that appears in that time, as with daily and monthly.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把表示时间的形容词转成名词，指在那个时间出现的东西，daily 与 monthly 都是如此。

items.cn: 英语 annual 最初指每年举行一次的宗教仪式。

abstract.en: See the same fairground return each September.

definition_zh: 年金；养老金；年金保险
definition_en: a fixed sum of money paid each year, or the contract providing it
core_image: 每年准时寄到的一笔钱：像一棵按时结果的树
scene: 退休教师打开信封，里面又是那笔固定的款项。The retired teacher lives on an annuity from her late husband's pension fund.
sceneCN: 这里 annuity 是「年金」（第 1 个义项：按年支付的固定款项）；句意为：退休教师靠亡夫养老基金支付的年金生活。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁短语借入，义为「每年」

senses.title: A yearly payment of money
senses.definition: a fixed sum paid once a year to a person
senses.definitionCN: 每年一次付给某人的固定款项
senses.example: The trust pays her an annuity of ten thousand dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 信托每年付给她一万美元年金。
senses.why: The Latin annus means year, so the word names a payment defined by the year.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 annus 意为「年」，该词即指以「年」为单位的支付。

senses.title: The contract or investment providing such payment
senses.definition: a financial contract that guarantees periodic payments, usually in retirement
senses.definitionCN: 保证定期给付的金融契约，多用于退休
senses.example: He converted his savings into a life annuity.
senses.exampleCN: 他把积蓄转换成了终身年金。
senses.why: The payment and the legal machine behind it share one name.
senses.whyCN: 支付行为与背后的法律装置共用一个名称。

senses.title: Payments more frequent than yearly
senses.definition: a series of equal periodic payments, even monthly or quarterly
senses.definitionCN: 等额的定期给付序列，即便按月或按季
senses.example: Most annuities now pay monthly rather than annually.
senses.exampleCN: 如今多数年金按月而非按年给付。
senses.why: The yearly frame stretched to fit any equal interval.
senses.whyCN: 「按年」的框架被拉伸以适配任何等距时段。

senses.title: A life annuity: income until death
senses.definition: an annuity that pays until the holder's death
senses.definitionCN: 支付至持有人去世为止的年金
senses.example: A life annuity removes the fear of outliving savings.
senses.exampleCN: 终身年金消除了「人还在、钱没了」的恐惧。
senses.why: The insurance pool trades a lump sum for a promise without an end date.
senses.whyCN: 保险池以一笔一次性款项换取一份没有截止日的承诺。

senses.title: A deferred annuity: payment that starts later
senses.definition: an annuity whose payments begin at a chosen future date
senses.definitionCN: 在选定的未来日期才开始给付的年金
senses.example: Her deferred annuity starts when she turns sixty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 她的递延年金在她六十五岁时开始给付。
senses.why: The promise can sleep for years before it starts paying.
senses.whyCN: 承诺可以先沉睡多年再开始兑现。

senses.title: An annuity in feudal history
senses.definition: a yearly grant of money from a lord, crown, or institution
senses.definitionCN: 领主、王室或机构授予的年度钱款
senses.example: The poet received a royal annuity in 1619.
senses.exampleCN: 这位诗人于 1619 年获得王室年俸。
senses.why: Before insurance, the crown itself was the payer of yearly sums.
senses.whyCN: 在保险出现之前，王室本身就是年款的支付者。

senses.title: Annuity as steady, reliable income
senses.definition: any reliable source of regular income, likened to an annuity
senses.definitionCN: 被比作年金的任何稳定定期收入
senses.example: The hit song became an annuity for its writer.
senses.exampleCN: 那首热门歌曲成了词作者的稳定财源。
senses.why: What pays regularly without further work feels like an annuity.
senses.whyCN: 无需再劳作仍定期入账之物，感觉便如年金。

senses.title: Annuity certain: payments for a fixed term
senses.definition: an annuity that pays for a set number of years, however long the holder lives
senses.definitionCN: 不论持有人寿命长短、给付固定年数的年金
senses.example: He chose an annuity certain for fifteen years.
senses.exampleCN: 他选择了为期十五年的定期年金。
senses.why: The promise can be bounded by years instead of by a lifespan.
senses.whyCN: 承诺的边界可以是「年数」而非「寿命」。

intro.en: Annuity is the Latin year turned into money: a payment that the calendar itself calls for.
intro.cn: annuity 是被金钱化的拉丁「年」：一笔由历法本身召唤的支付。

items.en: The root *at- meant to go, and the completed circuit became the year.
items.cn: 印欧词根 *at- 意为「行走」，走完一圈即为「年」，一般认为如此。

items.en: Annus meant year; the adjective annualis meant yearly.
items.cn: 拉丁语 annus 意为「年」，形容词 annualis 意为「每年的」。

normal.cn: annals 按年记录，annuity 按年支付：同根两向。

abstract.en: Picture a tree that drops the same number of coins into your yard every spring.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵每年春天往你院子里落下等量硬币的树。

abstract.en: See a calendar page turning, and with each turn a coin lands in a bowl.
abstract.cn: 想象日历每翻一页，一枚硬币落进碗里。

abstract.en: Feel the calm of a bill you never have to earn again.
abstract.cn: 感受一笔不必再去挣的钱带来的安心。

examples.en: She bought an annuity to secure her retirement income.
examples.cn: 她购买了年金以保障退休收入。

examples.en: The fellowship carries a generous annuity.
examples.cn: 该研究基金附带丰厚的年俸。

examples.en: Royalties from the textbook are his private annuity.
examples.cn: 教科书的版税是他私人的稳定财源。

sensesIntro.en: From the yearly payment, the word grows into contracts, insurance products, royal grants, and any metaphorical stream of steady money.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「年付之款」出发，词义生长为契约、保险产品、王室年赐，以及任何比喻性的稳定财源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same sum landing every year, like fruit in season
core.cn: 核心意象：每年准时落下的等额之款，如应季果实

branches.en: the payment itself, by year or by month

branches.cn: 历史上的王室或领主年赐

intro.cn: annuity 属于紧凑的 ann-「年」词族，所有成员都以「年」计时间。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin combined annus with the noun suffix -itas to name the yearly obligation.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语以 annus 加名词后缀 -itas 构成年付义务之名。

Civility and utility share this ending.

definition_zh: 阳极；正极
definition_en: the positively charged electrode by which electrons leave a device, or the electrode where oxidation occurs
core_image: 电流进出的门柱之一：阳极这边，电子动身离开
scene: 化学老师把铜片和锌片插进液体。Electrons flow from the anode through the wire to the cathode.
sceneCN: 这里 anode 是「阳极」（第 1 个义项：电流所经的电极之一）；句意为：电子从阳极经导线流向阴极。

pos.zh: 阳极；正极（电解中为发生氧化的一极）

derivatives.zh: anode + -ize，义为「对……作阳极氧化处理」
与 anode 相对造出的词，义为「阴极」，同 -ode 后缀

senses.title: The positive terminal of a cell or battery
senses.definition: the electrode through which conventional current enters a battery from outside
senses.definitionCN: 电流从外部进入电池所经的电极
senses.example: Connect the red wire to the anode of the battery.
senses.exampleCN: 把红线接到电池的正极。
senses.why: Faraday coined the word for the way up in a circuit, and the positive pole took it.
senses.whyCN: 法拉第为电路中的「上行之路」造了此词，正极获得了这个名字。

senses.title: The electrode where oxidation occurs in electrolysis
senses.definition: in electrolysis, the electrode at which negative ions discharge and oxidation happens
senses.definitionCN: 电解时负离子放电、发生氧化反应的电极
senses.example: Chlorine gas bubbles off at the anode.
senses.exampleCN: 氯气在阳极冒出气泡。
senses.why: Ions travel up toward the anode, the road named for ascending.
senses.whyCN: 离子向上行进至阳极，正如其名所示的「上行之路」。

senses.title: The electron-emitting electrode in a vacuum tube
senses.definition: in a vacuum tube, the plate that collects electrons emitted by the cathode
senses.definitionCN: 真空管中收集阴极发射电子的板极
senses.example: Old radios failed when the anode burned out.
senses.exampleCN: 旧收音机常因板极烧毁而失灵。
senses.why: The ascending road is where the electron journey ends.
senses.whyCN: 这条「上行之路」正是电子旅程的终点。

senses.title: An electrode in an X-ray tube
senses.definition: the metal target in an X-ray tube that the electron beam strikes
senses.definitionCN: X 射线管中电子束轰击的金属靶
senses.example: The rotating anode keeps the X-ray tube from melting.
senses.exampleCN: 旋转阳极防止 X 射线管过热熔化。
senses.why: Where the ascending electrons land, light is born.
senses.whyCN: 上行电子的落点，正是光产生之处。

senses.title: A sacrificial anode protecting metal from corrosion
senses.definition: a reactive metal electrode that corrodes instead of the protected structure
senses.definitionCN: 代替被保护结构发生腐蚀的活泼金属电极
senses.example: Sacrificial anodes protect the ship's hull underwater.
senses.exampleCN: 牺牲阳极在水下保护船体。
senses.why: One electrode gives itself up so the whole may last.
senses.whyCN: 一个电极自我牺牲，使整体得以长存。

senses.title: The positive electrode of an electrolytic cell in industry
senses.definition: the electrode used in industrial processes such as electroplating or smelting
senses.definitionCN: 电镀、冶炼等工业过程中使用的电极
senses.example: Aluminum smelting consumes carbon anodes steadily.
senses.exampleCN: 炼铝过程持续消耗碳阳极。
senses.why: Industry scales the laboratory cell to factory size, keeping the same poles.
senses.whyCN: 工业把实验室电解槽放大到工厂规模，而极的名称不变。

senses.title: Anode in diodes and semiconductors
senses.definition: the terminal of a diode at which forward current enters
senses.definitionCN: 二极管上正向电流流入的一端
senses.example: The LED lights only when wired anode to positive.
senses.exampleCN: 只有阳极接正极，LED 才会亮。
senses.why: Semiconductors inherit the battery's vocabulary for their two doors.
senses.whyCN: 半导体沿用了电池给它的两扇「门」所起的名称。

senses.title: Anode in welding and plasma work
senses.definition: the workpiece or electrode that acts as the positive pole in arc processes
senses.definitionCN: 电弧工艺中充当正极的工件或电极
senses.example: In this torch setup the workpiece is the anode.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种焊枪配置中，工件即为阳极。
senses.why: Every arc needs an up road and a down road for its charge.
senses.whyCN: 每条电弧都需要一上一下两条电荷之路。

intro.en: Anode is one of Michael Faraday's own coinages, built from Greek for a way up, chosen with the help of a classical scholar.
intro.cn: anode 是迈克尔·法拉第亲自创造的词，源自希腊语「上行之路」，是在一位古典学者的帮助下选定的。

items.en: The roots *h₁ed- (to go) and *upo- (up from under) are generally reconstructed behind Greek hodos and ana-.
items.cn: 一般认为希腊语 hodos 出自印欧词根 *h₁ed-（行走），ana- 出自 *upo-（自下而上），均为重构形式。

items.en: Anos meant up, and hodos meant way; the phrase pointed to a rising road.
items.cn: 希腊语 anos 意为「向上」，hodos 意为「路」，合指「上行之路」。

items.en: In 1834 Faraday, advised by William Whewell, coined anode and cathode for his electrochemistry papers.
items.cn: 1834 年，法拉第在威廉·休厄尔建议下，为其电化学论文创造了 anode 与 cathode。

items.en: The words spread through battery, electrolysis, and vacuum-tube technology.
items.cn: 这两个词随之进入电池、电解与真空管技术的语汇。

items.en: Anode now names the positive pole in batteries and the oxidation site in cells, with an established verb anodize.
items.cn: 如今 anode 既指电池正极，也指电解中发生氧化的一极，并衍生出动词 anodize。

note.en: Grouped by the shared -ode road-roots Faraday coined and by electrode neighbors.
note.cn: 按法拉第所造的同后缀「路」词与电极近义词分组。

entries.definitionCN: 阴极，与 anode 相对造出、共享 -ode 后缀

entries.definition: a conductor through which current enters or leaves

entries.definitionCN: 电池正极的日常说法，与 anode 在电池语境中同指

entries.definition: the anode of a vacuum tube, in trade jargon
entries.definitionCN: 板极，真空管行业对阳极的称呼

entries.definition: either end point of a circuit element
entries.definitionCN: 端子；接线端，泛指电路元件的两端

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek roots Faraday built on.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于法拉第所用的真实希腊词根。

normal.en: ana- (up) + hodos (way) = the way up: anode.
normal.cn: ana-（向上）+ hodos（路）= 上行之路：即 anode。

normal.en: Cathode is the matching way down, kata- meaning down.
normal.cn: cathode 是对应的下行之路，kata- 意为「向下」。

normal.en: Anions (negative ions) walk up to the anode in electrolysis.
normal.cn: 电解时阴离子「上行」走向阳极。

normal.en: Remember PANiC: Positive Anode, Negative Cathode, for batteries.
normal.cn: 电池口诀：正极阳极（PANiC 的 PA），负极阴极。

normal.en: Anodize means to treat metal as if at the anode, building an oxide layer.
normal.cn: anodize 指像在阳极那样对金属作氧化处理。

abstract.en: Picture an escalator for charges, going up through the anode door.
abstract.cn: 想象一道为电荷准备的自动扶梯，向上穿过阳极之门。

abstract.en: See a dull zinc block dissolving slowly beside a shiny ship's hull.
abstract.cn: 想象一块黯淡的锌块在闪亮的船体旁缓缓溶解。

abstract.en: Feel one pole pulling and the other pushing, the circuit breathing between them.
abstract.cn: 感受一极拉、一极推，电路在其间呼吸。

examples.en: Corrosion was stopped by fitting a magnesium anode.
examples.cn: 安装镁制阳极后腐蚀停止了。

examples.en: The anode of the diode must face the positive supply.
examples.cn: 二极管的阳极必须朝向电源正极。

examples.en: Aluminum parts are anodized at the anode to resist scratching.
examples.cn: 铝件在阳极作氧化处理以抗刮擦。

definition_zh: 异常；反常事物；不规则
definition_en: something that deviates from what is normal or expected
core_image: 整齐队伍里突然站歪的一个人：不合群的那一点
scene: 统计员盯着报表，一行数字格格不入。The warm winter was an anomaly in forty years of weather records.
sceneCN: 这里 anomaly 是「异常」（第 1 个义项：偏离常规的事物）；句意为：这个暖冬是四十年气象记录中的一次异常。

senses.title: A deviation from the normal or expected
senses.definition: a fact or event that differs from what standard rules or patterns predict
senses.definitionCN: 与常规规则或模式所预测不同的事实或事件
senses.example: The audit flagged one anomaly in the expense records.
senses.exampleCN: 审计在报销记录中发现一处异常。
senses.why: The Greek root means unequal or irregular, so anything off the rule is an anomaly.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根意为「不均、不规则」，凡不合规则者即为 anomaly。

senses.title: A congenital or biological irregularity
senses.definition: a structural irregularity present in a body or organism
senses.definitionCN: 身体或生物体中存在的结构性不规则
senses.example: The scan revealed a minor cardiac anomaly.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描发现一处轻微的心脏异常。
senses.why: Bodies too can stand out of line from the standard pattern.
senses.whyCN: 身体同样可能偏离标准形态而「站歪」。

senses.title: An astronomical irregularity of position or motion
senses.definition: in astronomy, the angle defining position on an orbit, or any orbital irregularity
senses.definitionCN: 天文学中界定轨道位置的角，或轨道上的不规则性
senses.example: Mercury's perihelion anomaly puzzled astronomers for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 水星近日点反常困扰了天文学家数十年。
senses.why: Planets that refuse the perfect circle were the first named irregulars.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝完美圆形的行星是最早被冠以「不规则」之名者。

senses.title: An oddity among people or things
senses.definition: a person or thing that does not fit its class
senses.definitionCN: 不属于其类别的人或物
senses.example: Among the brick houses, the glass tower is an anomaly.
senses.exampleCN: 在砖房之间，玻璃塔楼是个异类。
senses.why: What breaks the row invites the Greek word for unevenness.
senses.whyCN: 破坏队列之物自然招来希腊语的「不均」之名。

senses.title: An anomaly in language or grammar
senses.definition: an irregular form or usage in a language
senses.definitionCN: 语言中不规则的形式或用法
senses.example: The verb to be is the great anomaly of English grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 动词 be 是英语语法中最大的不规则现象。
senses.why: Grammar, like planets, keeps a few unruly members.
senses.whyCN: 语法如行星，也总有几个不服管教的成员。

senses.title: An anomaly in law or institutions
senses.definition: an inconsistency or contradiction within rules or institutions
senses.definitionCN: 规则或制度内部的不一致或矛盾
senses.example: The old statute created an anomaly between the two courts.
senses.exampleCN: 旧法令造成两个法院之间的制度不一致。
senses.why: Systems built by hand always leave an uneven joint somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 人为建造的系统总会在某处留下不齐的接缝。

senses.title: An anomaly as clue or discovery
senses.definition: an unexpected result that points toward a discovery
senses.definitionCN: 指向新发现的意外结果
senses.example: The anomaly in the data led to a new particle.
senses.exampleCN: 数据中的异常导致了一种新粒子的发现。
senses.why: The irregular is where the rule book runs out and science begins.
senses.whyCN: 不规则之处正是规则手册失效、科学起步之地。

senses.title: Anomalous weather or market behavior
senses.definition: an abnormal pattern in climate or markets that breaks the trend
senses.definitionCN: 打破趋势的气候或市场异常模式
senses.example: The frost in April was an agricultural anomaly.
senses.exampleCN: 四月的霜冻是一次农业气象反常。
senses.why: When the usual rhythm stumbles, the word for unevenness returns.
senses.whyCN: 当惯常节奏绊了一跤，「不均」一词便再度登场。

intro.en: Anomaly is Greek for unevenness: the state of not being alike, the lump in the smooth field.
intro.cn: anomaly 在希腊语中即「不均」：彼此不一的状态，平坦原野上的那处隆起。

items.en: The root *h₂emos meant belonging to a group, giving Greek homalos, even and level.
items.cn: 一般认为印欧词根 *h₂emos 意为「属于一群」，派生希腊语 homalos（均匀的、平的）。

items.en: Anomalos joined a- (not) with homalos (even), meaning unequal or irregular.
items.cn: 希腊语 anomalos 由 a-（不）加 homalos（均匀）构成，意为「不均的、不规则的」。

items.en: Anomalía named the irregularity itself, used by astronomers for orbital unevenness.
items.cn: 后希腊语 anomalía 指不规则性本身，天文学家用以指轨道的不均匀。

items.en: Latin borrowed anomalía as anomalia, keeping the astronomical use.
items.cn: 拉丁语将 anomalía 借为 anomalia，保留其天文用法。

items.en: English took anomaly from Latin around 1600, and the adjective anomalous followed for general irregularity.
items.cn: 英语约 1600 年自拉丁语借入 anomaly，形容词 anomalous 随之用于泛指不规则。

note.en: Grouped by shared roots and by words nearby in the field of the irregular.
note.cn: 按共享词根与「不规则」义场的近义词分组。

entries.definitionCN: 偏离正轨；失常，较正式且略带贬义

normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的希腊部件 a- 与 homalos。

normal.en: Same homalos family: homogeneous, homologous, all about sameness.

normal.en: The adjective is anomalous; the plural is anomalies.
normal.cn: 形容词为 anomalous；复数为 anomalies。

normal.en: Astronomers still use true anomaly and mean anomaly for orbits.
normal.cn: 天文学至今仍用 true anomaly 与 mean anomaly 描述轨道。

normal.en: An anemic system lacks blood; an anomalous result lacks normality.
normal.cn: anemic 系统缺血；anomalous 结果缺「正常」。

abstract.en: Picture one house on the street painted bright orange among gray ones.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色房子之间一栋亮橙色的房子。

abstract.en: See a heartbeat monitor flat and calm, then one sudden spike.
abstract.cn: 想象平稳的心电监护线，突然跳起一个尖峰。

abstract.en: Feel a stone in the shoe: small, off-pattern, impossible to ignore.
abstract.cn: 感受鞋里的一粒石子：小、不合律、无法忽视。

examples.en: The temperature spike was an anomaly that the models could not explain.
examples.cn: 气温骤升是模型无法解释的异常。

examples.en: Every dataset contains anomalies worth investigating.
examples.cn: 每个数据集都含有值得调查的异常值。

examples.en: His calm reaction was an anomaly in the panicking crowd.
examples.cn: 在惊慌的人群中，他的镇定是个异类。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，哪me里」——咦，这数据哪里不对劲？发现 anomaly（异常）时的心声。

sensesIntro.en: From Greek unevenness, the noun marks odd data, odd bodies, odd planets, odd grammar, and every outlier that breaks the row.
sensesIntro.cn: 从希腊语的「不均」出发，名词标记奇异数据、异常身体、不规则行星、例外语法，以及一切破坏队列的离群者。

definition_en: having no name given or known, or lacking any distinctive character

senses.title: With no name given
senses.definition: written, given, or done by someone who does not reveal their name
senses.definitionCN: 由不透露姓名的人所写、所给或所做的
senses.example: The donation came from an anonymous reader.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔捐款来自一位匿名读者。
senses.why: Greek an- means 'without' and onoma means 'name', so anonymous literally describes something that arrives without a name attached.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 an- 意为「无」，onoma 意为「名字」，所以 anonymous 字面就是指送来时没有附上名字的东西。

senses.title: With no known author
senses.definition: used of a work or person whose name is unknown rather than deliberately withheld
senses.definitionCN: 用于作品或人，其名字是不为人知，而非有意隐去
senses.example: The painting was long thought to be by an anonymous artist.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画长期被认为出自一位无名画家之手。
senses.why: The same word covers both hiding a name and simply not knowing it, because in either case no name is available.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指隐去名字，也指根本不知道名字，因为两种情况下都拿不到名字。

senses.title: Without distinctive character
senses.definition: lacking any feature that would make a place, object, or experience memorable
senses.definitionCN: 缺少任何能让地方、物件或经历留下印象的特点
senses.example: They spent the night in an anonymous hotel near the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在机场附近一家毫无特色的旅馆过了一夜。
senses.why: If a thing has no name you can recall, it feels interchangeable, and that feeling of facelessness is the extended sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西没有你能记住的名字，它就显得可以随便替换，这种面目模糊的感觉就是延伸义。

definition_en: active hostility or opposition between people or forces
core_image: 拔河绳的两端：两股力正面对顶，谁也不让
scene: 谈判桌两侧，双方代表的笑容都僵住了。The antagonism between the two departments delayed the project for months.
sceneCN: 这里 antagonism 是「对抗、敌对」（第 1 个义项：主动的敌对关系）；句意为：两个部门之间的对立使项目拖延了数月。

同根名词，义为「对手；拮抗剂」

senses.title: Active hostility between parties
senses.definition: openly hostile feeling or relations between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 人与人或群体之间公开的敌对情绪或关系
senses.example: The antagonism between the rival editors shaped the paper's history.
senses.exampleCN: 两位主编之间的对立塑造了这份报纸的历史。
senses.why: The Greek root means to struggle against, so the word names the struggle itself.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为「与……斗争」，该词即指这种斗争关系本身。

senses.title: Opposition of forces or principles
senses.definition: the opposition of impersonal forces, interests, or principles
senses.definitionCN: 非人格化的力量、利益或原则之间的对抗
senses.example: There is a built-in antagonism between profit and safety budgets.
senses.exampleCN: 利润与安全预算之间存在天然的对立。
senses.why: Two directions on one rope pull apart even without hatred.
senses.whyCN: 同一根绳上的两个方向，即使没有仇恨也会彼此拉开。

senses.title: Physiological opposition of agents
senses.definition: the opposing action of muscles, drugs, or biological agents
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉、药物或生物制剂之间的对抗性作用
senses.example: Flexor and extensor muscles work by antagonism.
senses.exampleCN: 屈肌与伸肌通过拮抗协作。
senses.why: The struggle metaphor became literal in the laboratory.
senses.whyCN: 「斗争」的比喻在实验室里变成了字面事实。

senses.title: Antagonism as a class or social divide
senses.definition: deep-seated hostility dividing social classes or factions
senses.definitionCN: 划分社会阶级或派别的深刻敌意
senses.example: The strike exposed the antagonism between owners and workers.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工暴露了劳资之间的对立。
senses.why: Struggle scaled from persons to whole social bodies.
senses.whyCN: 斗争从个人放大到整个社会肌体。

senses.title: Feeling of ill will behind opposition
senses.definition: the hostile emotion underlying opposition
senses.definitionCN: 对抗背后所存的敌对情绪
senses.example: His questions carried no antagonism, only curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 他的提问并无敌意，只有好奇。
senses.why: Antagonism can stay a feeling, a stance of the mind not yet a fight.
senses.whyCN: 对抗可以只停留在情绪，是尚未开打的心理姿态。

senses.title: Antagonism in ecology or chemistry
senses.definition: the interaction in which one organism or substance inhibits another
senses.definitionCN: 一种生物或物质抑制另一种的相互作用
senses.example: Fungal antagonism keeps the mold population in check.
senses.exampleCN: 真菌间的拮抗作用抑制了霉菌数量。
senses.why: Nature too stages struggles, and science named them with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 自然界同样上演斗争，科学以同一个词命名之。

senses.title: Antagonism toward change or ideas
senses.definition: resistance or hostility directed at proposals or innovations
senses.definitionCN: 针对提案或革新的抵触与敌意
senses.example: The proposal met instant antagonism from the old guard.
senses.exampleCN: 提案立即遭到保守派的抵触。
senses.why: Every new direction is a pull against the settled one.
senses.whyCN: 每个新方向都是对既有方向的一次拉扯。

senses.title: Antagonisms as recurring conflicts
senses.definition: multiple opposed relations within a system or history
senses.definitionCN: 系统或历史中多重的对立关系
senses.example: The novel weaves the antagonisms of three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 小说交织着三代人之间的多重对抗。
senses.why: Struggles rarely come alone; they collect into structures.
senses.whyCN: 斗争很少单独出现，它们会聚成结构。

intro.en: Antagonism comes from the Greek word for a competitor or wrestler, one who struggles against another for a prize.
intro.cn: antagonism 源自希腊语「竞争者、角力士」一词，指为奖品与他人相搏之人。

items.en: The root *deh₃- (to divide out) underlies Greek agein, to drive or lead, generally reconstructed.
items.cn: 一般认为希腊语 agein（驱动、引领）出自印欧词根 *deh₃-（分派），属重构。

items.en: Agon meant contest or assembly for games; ant- added the sense of against; antagonistes meant a rival.
items.cn: 希腊语 agon 意为「竞技、赛会」；ant- 表「对抗」；antagonistes 意为「对手」。

items.en: Antagonizesthai meant to struggle against, in body or in politics.
items.cn: 后希腊语 antagonizesthai 意为「与……斗争」，可用于体格或政治。

items.en: English adopted antagonism in the seventeenth century, first of bodily opposition, then of minds and classes.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪借入 antagonism，先指身体对抗，后指思想与阶级的对立。

items.en: The word now spans social conflict, muscle physiology, and drug interactions.
items.cn: 如今该词覆盖社会冲突、肌肉生理学与药物相互作用。

note.en: Grouped by the shared agon root and by neighboring hostility words.
note.cn: 按共享 agon 词根与敌对近义词分组。

normalIntro.en: These hooks rest on the real Greek agon, the contest.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的希腊词根 agon（竞技）。

normal.en: anti- (against) + agon (contest) = one who struggles against: antagonist, hence antagonism.
normal.cn: anti-（对抗）+ agon（竞技）= 与之相搏者：antagonist，进而 antagonism。

normal.en: Same agon family: agony, protagonist, agonistic.
normal.cn: agon 同族：agony、protagonist、agonistic。

normal.en: The antagonist of a story opposes the protagonist.
normal.cn: 故事里的 antagonist 与 protagonist 相对。

normal.en: In pharmacology, an antagonist blocks a receptor's action.
normal.cn: 药理学中 antagonist 指阻断受体作用的拮抗剂。

normal.en: Feel the tug-of-war image: antagonism is the rope strained from both ends.
normal.cn: 记住拔河的画面：antagonism 是两端绷紧的绳。

abstract.en: Picture two rams meeting head-on on a narrow ledge.
abstract.cn: 想象两只公羊在窄岩台上头顶头相撞。

abstract.en: See a courtroom with two tables turned to face each other.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭上两张相对而设的桌子。

abstract.en: Feel a flexed arm: one muscle fights the other so the limb can move.
abstract.cn: 感受屈起的手臂：一肌与另一肌相抗，肢体方能运动。

examples.en: Years of antagonism ended with a handshake at the border.
examples.cn: 多年的对立以边境上的一次握手告终。

examples.en: There was open antagonism between the two laboratories.
examples.cn: 两个实验室之间存在公开的对立。

examples.en: The drug works by antagonism against the natural hormone.
examples.cn: 这种药通过对天然激素的拮抗发挥作用。

scene: 拳击台上，聚光灯打在两个身影之间。In the final round, the champion finally wore down his antagonist.

senses.title: An opponent in a struggle or contest
senses.definition: a person who actively fights or competes against another
senses.definitionCN: 主动与人对立或竞争的人
senses.example: Negotiators from both sides sat down as old antagonists.
senses.exampleCN: 双方的谈判者以宿敌身份坐下。
senses.why: The Greek word named the wrestler at the other end of the sand floor.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原词即指沙地擂台另一端的角力者。

senses.title: The opposing character in a narrative
senses.definition: the character who opposes the protagonist in a story
senses.definitionCN: 故事中与主角相对立的角色
senses.example: The antagonist here is not a villain but the sea itself.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的反派不是恶人，而是大海本身。
senses.why: Every drama needs a force against the hero's aim.
senses.whyCN: 每出戏都需要一个阻碍主角目标的力量。

senses.title: An opposing force of nature or circumstance
senses.definition: an impersonal power that works against a person's efforts
senses.definitionCN: 阻碍人努力的非物质力量
senses.example: The mountain was the climber's true antagonist.
senses.exampleCN: 这座山才是登山者真正的对手。
senses.why: Opposition need not have a face; any resisting force qualifies.
senses.whyCN: 对抗不必有面孔，任何阻力都算数。

senses.title: A muscle that opposes another's action
senses.definition: a muscle that acts against the movement of another muscle
senses.definitionCN: 与另一肌肉动作相对抗的肌肉
senses.example: The biceps works against its antagonist, the triceps.
senses.exampleCN: 肱二头肌与其拮抗肌肱三头肌相对作用。
senses.why: Anatomy borrowed the wrestling image for paired muscles.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学借角力意象命名成对的肌肉。

senses.title: A drug that blocks a receptor's action
senses.definition: a substance that blocks or dampens the effect of another, as at a receptor
senses.definitionCN: 在受体处阻断或抑制另一物质作用的物质
senses.example: Naloxone is an opioid antagonist used in emergencies.
senses.exampleCN: 纳洛酮是用于急救的阿片受体拮抗剂。
senses.why: Pharmacology kept the wrestler: one agent throws the other off the receptor.
senses.whyCN: 药理学保留了角力者：一种药剂把另一种从受体上「摔下」。

senses.title: A rival in argument or debate
senses.definition: an opponent in discussion or controversy
senses.definitionCN: 讨论或论战中的对方
senses.example: He greeted his antagonist across the editorial page each week.
senses.exampleCN: 他每周都在评论版与论敌隔纸交锋。
senses.why: Contests moved from the sand floor to the printed page.
senses.whyCN: 角力从沙地擂台移到了印刷版面。

senses.title: A political or national opponent
senses.definition: a rival power, party, or statesman in public struggle
senses.definitionCN: 公共斗争中的对手国家、政党或政治人物
senses.example: The treaty softened relations with an old antagonist.
senses.exampleCN: 条约缓和了与宿敌国的关系。
senses.why: Whole states can enter the arena as wrestlers once did.
senses.whyCN: 整个国家可以像当年的角力士一样走进竞技场。

senses.title: An antagonist to something: the counter-agent
senses.definition: any agent defined by working against something else
senses.definitionCN: 以「对抗某物」定义的一切动因
senses.example: Skepticism is the natural antagonist of blind faith.
senses.exampleCN: 怀疑是盲信的天然对抗者。
senses.why: Once the word means opposer, even ideas can step onto the mat.
senses.whyCN: 一旦该词意为「对立者」，连观念也能登上擂台。

intro.en: Antagonist began as the Greek name for the other wrestler, the one who struggles against you for the prize.
intro.cn: antagonist 原是希腊语对「另一名角力士」的称呼，即为奖品与你相搏之人。

items.en: The root *deh₃- (to divide, apportion) is generally reconstructed behind Greek agein, to drive or lead.
items.cn: 一般认为希腊语 agein（驱动）出自印欧词根 *deh₃-（分派），属重构。

items.en: Agon meant a contest; with anti- (against), antagonistēs meant the opposing combatant.
items.cn: 希腊语 agon 意为「竞技」；加 anti-（对抗）后，antagonistēs 意为「对方搏斗者」。

items.en: Aristotle used antagonistēs of rivals in drama and politics alike.
items.cn: 亚里士多德即用 antagonistēs 称戏剧与政治中的对手。

items.en: English adopted antagonist in the sixteenth century for combatants and debaters.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入 antagonist，用于搏斗者与论辩者。

items.en: Literary theory fixed the villain sense, medicine added muscles and receptor blockers.
items.cn: 文学理论固定了「反派」义，医学则添入拮抗肌与受体拮抗剂。

abstract.en: Picture two chess players leaning over the same board, eyes locked.

examples.en: The detective and his antagonist match wits for six chapters.

examples.en: Give the receptor antagonist before symptoms worsen.

senses.title: To make someone into an enemy
senses.definition: to cause a person to feel or show hostility toward you
senses.definitionCN: 使人对你产生或表现出敌意
senses.example: The manager antagonized the whole staff with one memo.
senses.exampleCN: 经理用一纸备忘录把全体员工都得罪了。
senses.why: The wrestling root turns a partner into an opponent.
senses.whyCN: 角力词根把「同侪」变成了「对手」。

senses.title: To provoke by words or actions
senses.definition: to irritate someone deliberately or carelessly
senses.definitionCN: 故意或无意地刺激、惹怒他人
senses.example: He enjoys antagonizing the umpires from the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 他喜欢在场边挑衅裁判。
senses.why: A shove at the shoulder is how the match begins.
senses.whyCN: 朝肩膀一推，正是比赛的开始。

senses.title: To lose support by offending
senses.definition: to alienate people whose goodwill you need
senses.definitionCN: 疏远那些你本需要其好感的人
senses.example: The mayor antagonized the unions before the election.
senses.exampleCN: 市长在选举前得罪了工会。
senses.why: Every push creates a pusher-shaped hole where friendship used to be.
senses.whyCN: 每一次推搡都会在友谊的原址留下一个空洞。

senses.title: To block the action of a substance in pharmacology
senses.definition: to inhibit or block the effect of a drug or natural chemical
senses.definitionCN: 抑制或阻断药物或天然化学物质的作用
senses.example: This compound antagonizes the histamine response.
senses.exampleCN: 这种化合物拮抗组胺反应。
senses.why: Chemistry stages the wrestling match at the receptor.
senses.whyCN: 化学把角力赛搬到了受体上。

senses.title: To counteract a physiological process
senses.definition: to work against a bodily process or muscle action
senses.definitionCN: 对抗身体过程或肌肉作用
senses.example: The stretch reflex is antagonized by conscious effort.
senses.exampleCN: 意识努力可对抗牵张反射。
senses.why: The body hosts its own contests between processes.
senses.whyCN: 身体内部本就上演着各过程的角力。

senses.title: To act in opposition to an idea or policy
senses.definition: to position oneself or one's actions against a principle or plan
senses.definitionCN: 使自己或行动与原则、计划相对立
senses.example: The new rules antagonize everything the founders stood for.
senses.exampleCN: 新规与创始人的一切主张背道而驰。
senses.why: Opposition extends from persons to the things they stand for.
senses.whyCN: 对抗从人扩展到人所代表的东西。

senses.title: To antagonize a group into action
senses.definition: to provoke a group so that it organizes against you
senses.definitionCN: 把一个群体激怒到组织起来反对你
senses.example: The layoffs antagonized workers into forming a union.
senses.exampleCN: 裁员把工人激怒成了工会。
senses.why: A provoked opponent is made, not born.
senses.whyCN: 对手是被制造出来的，而非天生。

senses.title: To be easily antagonized
senses.definition: to become hostile readily upon slight offense
senses.definitionCN: 因轻微冒犯便轻易生出敌意
senses.example: The old professor antagonized easily after his retirement.
senses.exampleCN: 退休后，老教授变得容易被触怒。
senses.why: The verb can describe the striker or the tinder.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词既可描述划火柴者，也可描述干草本身。

intro.en: Antagonize is the verb of the wrestling family: to turn someone into your antagonist.
intro.cn: antagonize 是角力词族的动词：把某人变成你的 antagonist。

items.en: The root *deh₃- (to apportion) is generally reconstructed behind Greek agein, to drive.
items.cn: 一般认为希腊语 agein（驱动）出自印欧词根 *deh₃-（分派），属重构。

items.en: Antagonizesthai meant to struggle against, built on agon, the contest.
items.cn: 希腊语 antagonizesthai 意为「与……相争」，建立在 agon（竞技）之上。

items.en: The middle-voice verb covered contests of body and of politics.
items.cn: 后希腊语的中动态动词涵盖体格与政治之争。

items.en: English formed the verb antagonize in the seventeenth century from the Greek verb's sense.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪依希腊动词之义造出 antagonize。

items.en: Everyday use now favors the social sense, while pharmacology keeps the blocking sense technical.
items.cn: 如今日常多用其社交义，药理学则保留「阻断」的技术义。

note.en: Grouped by the shared agon root and by nearby provocation words.
note.cn: 按共享 agon 词根与「挑衅」近义词分组。

entries.definition: the opponent that antagonizing creates
entries.definitionCN: 对手，antagonize 的结果名词，同根

entries.definition: the hostility that results
entries.definitionCN: 敌对（状态），同根名词

entries.definition: the main character, whom careless acts may turn antagonist
entries.definitionCN: 主角，同根对词

entries.definition: to make someone feel isolated or unfriendly
entries.definitionCN: 疏远；使不和，强调关系变冷

entries.definition: to stimulate anger or action deliberately
entries.definitionCN: 挑衅；激起，强调主动引发

entries.definition: to annoy mildly or persistently
entries.definitionCN: 激怒；使烦躁，程度较轻

normalIntro.en: These hooks rest on the real agon root and its family.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的 agon 词根及其词族。

normal.en: To antagonize someone is to make them your antagonist.
normal.cn: antagonize 某人就是使其成为你的 antagonist。

normal.en: Same root chain: agon, antagonist, antagonism, antagonize.
normal.cn: 同根链：agon → antagonist → antagonism → antagonize。

normal.en: Provoke creates anger; antagonize creates an opponent.
normal.cn: provoke 引发怒火；antagonize 制造对手。

normal.en: In pharmacy, antagonize means to block a receptor.
normal.cn: 药学中 antagonize 意为阻断受体。

normal.en: Politicians are warned never to antagonize the press.
normal.cn: 政客常被告诫切勿 antagonize（得罪）媒体。

abstract.en: Picture a hand flicking a sleeping dog's ear.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻弹熟睡狗的耳朵。

abstract.en: See a match head dragged along the rough strip.
abstract.cn: 想象火柴头沿粗糙条面划过。

abstract.en: Feel the moment a colleague stops smiling at your joke.
abstract.cn: 感受同事不再为你的玩笑发笑的那一刻。

examples.en: Don't antagonize the judge with that tone.
examples.cn: 别用那种口吻激怒法官。

examples.en: The drug antagonizes the effects of the sedative.
examples.cn: 这种药会拮抗镇静剂的作用。

examples.en: He managed to antagonize both landlords and tenants in one week.
examples.cn: 他一周内把房东房客都得罪了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺太哥恼伊」——俺把大哥惹恼了，伊人成了对手，正是 antagonize（激怒、使敌对）。

root: 希腊语 anti-（对抗）+ agōn（竞技，一般认为出自印欧词根 *deh₃-「分派」）→ antagonizesthai「与……相争」→ 英语 antagonize（17 世纪，依希腊动词义造出）。

sensesIntro.en: From turning a partner into a wrestler, the verb covers social provocation, lost goodwill, and the blocking of drugs and bodily processes.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把同侪变成角力士」出发，动词覆盖社交挑衅、失去人心，以及药物与生理过程的阻断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the flick that turns a bystander into a fighter
core.cn: 核心意象：把旁观者激成对手的那一弹指

branches.en: blocking at the level of chemistry and body
branches.cn: 化学与身体层面的阻断

branches.en: the tinder as well as the match

intro.en: The verb is built like its family: a Greek prefix and root plus an English verb ending.
intro.cn: 该动词与其词族构词一致：希腊前缀、词根加英语动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Though Greek in origin, it declines like a regular English verb.
latinIntro.cn: 虽源自希腊语，其变位却如规则英语动词。

items.example: Loud chewing irritates her.
